body.translated_text: <s>Kāvyādarśa</s> of the teacher <s>Daṇḍin</s>

children.text: manase ramatāṃ nityaṃ sarvaśuklā sarasvatī // DKd_1.1 //
children.translated_text: all-white, delight in my mind forever. //<s>DKd</s> 1.1//

body.translated_text: May <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the swan-bride of the lotus-face of the four-faced [<s>Brahmā</s>],

children.text: yathāsāmarthyam asmābhiḥ kriyate kāvyalakṣaṇam // DKd_1.2 //
children.translated_text: the science of poetics (<s>kāvyalakṣaṇa</s>) is composed by us to the best of our ability. //<s>DKd</s> 1.2//

body.translated_text: Having gathered together the earlier treatises and having observed actual practice,

children.text: vācām eva prasādena lokayātrā pravartate // DKd_1.3 //
children.translated_text: it is through the grace of speech alone that the course of worldly affairs proceeds. //<s>DKd</s> 1.3//

body.translated_text: Here, among the well-educated, those instructed by the learned, and the learned themselves — in every case,

children.text: yadi śabdāhavayaṃ jyotir āsaṃsārān na dīpyate // DKd_1.4 //
children.translated_text: if this light called 'word' did not shine forth throughout the cycle of existence. //<s>DKd</s> 1.4//

body.translated_text: This entire triple world would become utterly blind darkness,

children.text: teṣām asaṃnidhāne 'pi na svayaṃ paśya naśyati // DKd_1.5 //
children.translated_text: does not by itself perish even in their absence. //<s>DKd</s> 1.5//

body.translated_text: The reflected image of the first king's glory, having reached the mirror of literature,

body.text: gaur gauḥ kāmadughā samyak prayuktā smaryate budhaiḥ &

children.text: duṣprayuktā punār gotvaṃ prayoktuḥ saiva śaṃsati // DKd_1.6 //
children.translated_text: but improperly used, that very [word] proclaims the cow-ness [i.e. stupidity] of the user. //<s>DKd</s> 1.6//

body.translated_text: A word is like a wish-fulfilling cow: when properly employed, the wise remember it as yielding [all desires];

body.text: tad alpam api nopekṣyaṃ kāvye duṣṭaṃ kathaṃ cana &

children.text: syād vapuḥ sundaram api śvitreṇaikena durbhagam // DKd_1.7 //
children.translated_text: a body, however beautiful, becomes unfortunate by even a single patch of leucoderma. //<s>DKd</s> 1.7//

body.translated_text: Therefore, even a small fault in poetry should never be disregarded;

children.text: kim andhasyādhikāro 'sti rūpabhedopalabdhiṣu // DKd_1.8 //
children.translated_text: Does a blind person have any authority in perceiving distinctions of form? //<s>DKd</s> 1.8//

body.translated_text: How can a person ignorant of the science distinguish merits from faults?

body.text: ataḥ prajānāṃ (vl. padānāṃ) vyutpattim abhisaṃdhāya sūrayaḥ &

children.text: vācāṃ vicitramārgāṇāṃ nibabandhuḥ kriyāvidhiṃ // DKd_1.9 //
children.translated_text: have composed the science of practice (<s>kriyāvidhi</s>) for the diverse paths of speech. //<s>DKd</s> 1.9//

body.translated_text: Therefore, with the aim of educating people (or: [establishing] the derivation of words), the learned

body.text: taiḥ śarīraṃ ca kāvyānām alaṃkārāś ca darśitāḥ &

children.text: śarīraṃ tāvad iṣṭārthavyavacchinnā padāvalī // DKd_1.10 //
children.translated_text: the body, for its part, is a sequence of words delimited by the intended meaning. //<s>DKd</s> 1.10//

body.translated_text: By them, both the body of poems and the ornaments have been shown;

body.text: padyaṃ gadyaṃ ca miśraṃ ca tat tridhaiva vyavasthitam &

children.text: padyaṃ catuṣpadī tac ca vṛttaṃ jātir iti dvidhā // DKd_1.11 //
children.translated_text: verse is a four-line stanza, and that is of two kinds: <s>vṛtta</s> (metrically regulated) and <s>jāti</s> (based on <s>mātrā</s>-count). //<s>DKd</s> 1.11//

body.translated_text: Verse (<s>padya</s>), prose (<s>gadya</s>), and mixed (<s>miśra</s>) — it is established as exactly threefold;

children.text: sā vidyā naur vivikṣūṇāṃ gambhīraṃ kāvyasāgaram // DKd_1.12 //
children.translated_text: that science is a boat for those who wish to explore the deep ocean of poetry. //<s>DKd</s> 1.12//

body.translated_text: In the 'Consideration of Metres' (<s>Chandoviciti</s>), the entire elaboration of that [topic] has been demonstrated;

body.text: muktakaṃ kulakaṃ koṣaḥ saṃghāta iti tādṛśaḥ &

children.text: sargabandhāṃśarūpatvād anuktaḥ padyavistaraḥ // DKd_1.13 //
children.translated_text: varieties of verse have not been mentioned, since they are partial forms of the <s>sargabandha</s> (canto-composition). //<s>DKd</s> 1.13//

body.translated_text: <s>Muktaka</s> (independent stanzas), <s>kulaka</s> (verse-clusters), <s>koṣa</s> (anthologies), <s>saṃghāta</s> (verse-sequences) — such

children.text: āśīrnamaskriyā vastunirdeśo vāpi tanmukham // DKd_1.14 //
children.translated_text: its opening is a benediction, a salutation, or a statement of the subject-matter. //<s>DKd</s> 1.14//

body.translated_text: A <s>sargabandha</s> is called a <s>mahākāvya</s> (great poem). Its characteristics [are as follows]:

children.text: caturvargaphalāyattaṃ caturudāttanāyakam // DKd_1.15 //
children.translated_text: aiming at the four goals of life (<s>caturvarga</s>), with a noble hero of four types; //<s>DKd</s> 1.15//

body.translated_text: Arising from a narrative of legend (<s>itihāsa</s>) or otherwise, having a virtuous basis,

children.text: udyānasalilakṛīḍāmadhupānaratotsavaiḥ // DKd_1.16 //
children.translated_text: with garden-sports, water-sports, drinking-bouts, and love-festivals; //<s>DKd</s> 1.16//

body.translated_text: with descriptions of cities, oceans, mountains, seasons, the moon, the sun, and [their] risings;

children.text: mantradūtaprayāṇājināyakābhyudayair api // DKd_1.17 //
children.translated_text: with councils, messengers, marches, battles, and the hero's triumphs; //<s>DKd</s> 1.17//

body.translated_text: with separations, weddings, and descriptions of the birth of princes;

children.text: sargair anativistīrṇaiḥ śravyavṛttaiḥ susaṃdhibhiḥ // DKd_1.18 //
children.translated_text: with cantos not overly extended, having pleasing metres and proper junctures; //<s>DKd</s> 1.18//

body.translated_text: adorned, not abbreviated, pervaded throughout by <s>rasas</s> (sentiments) and <s>bhāvas</s> (emotions),

children.text: kāvyaṃ kalpāntarasthāyi jāyate sad alaṃkṛti // DKd_1.19 //
children.translated_text: such well-ornamented poetry endures until the end of a cosmic age. //<s>DKd</s> 1.19//

body.translated_text: furnished everywhere with varied episodes, delighting the world —

body.text: nyūnam apy atra yaiḥ kaiś cid aṅgaiḥ kāvyaṃ na duṣyati &

children.text: yady upātteṣu saṃpattir ārādhayati tadvidhaḥ // DKd_1.20 //
children.translated_text: if those that are employed are perfected — such a [poem] pleases the connoisseur. //<s>DKd</s> 1.20//

body.translated_text: Even if deficient in some of these elements, a poem is not spoiled,

body.text: guṇataḥ prāg upanyasya nāyakaṃ tena vidviṣām &

children.text: nirākaraṇam ity eṣa mārgaḥ prakṛtisundaraḥ // DKd_1.21 //
children.translated_text: the defeat of [his] enemies — this is the path that is naturally beautiful. //<s>DKd</s> 1.21//

body.translated_text: First presenting the hero in terms of [his] virtues, and through him [depicting]

children.text: tajjayān nāyakotkarṣakathanaṃ ca dhinoti naḥ // DKd_1.22 //
children.translated_text: and then narrating the hero's superiority through [the enemy's] defeat — that too delights us. //<s>DKd</s> 1.22//

body.translated_text: Describing even the enemy's lineage, valor, learning, and other [qualities],

children.text: iti tasya prabhedau dvau tayor ākhyāyikā kila // DKd_1.23 //
children.translated_text: are its two types — among these, the <s>ākhyāyikā</s> is [characterized as follows]: //<s>DKd</s> 1.23//

body.translated_text: A continuous flow of words without verse-feet is prose; <s>ākhyāyikā</s> (narrative) and <s>kathā</s> (story)

children.text: svaguṇāviṣkriyādoṣo nātrā bhūrtārthaśaṃsinaḥ // DKd_1.24 //
children.translated_text: the fault of self-praise does not apply to one who relates real events. //<s>DKd</s> 1.24//

body.translated_text: the story is narrated by the hero himself, or by the hero and another;

body.text: api tv aniyamo dṛṣṭas tatrāpy anyair udīraṇāt &

children.text: anyo vaktā svayaṃ veti kīdṛg vā bhedakāraṇam (vl. lakṣaṇam) // DKd_1.25 //
children.translated_text: whether another is the narrator or oneself — what kind of distinguishing criterion is that? //<s>DKd</s> 1.25//

body.translated_text: However, an absence of fixed rule is observed there too, because of narration by others;

body.text: vaktraṃ cāparavaktraṃ ca socchvāsatvaṃ ca bhedakam &

children.text: cihnam ākhyāyikāyāś cet prasaṅgena kathāsv api // DKd_1.26 //
children.translated_text: are the distinguishing marks of an <s>ākhyāyikā</s>, they are also found incidentally in <s>kathās</s>. //<s>DKd</s> 1.26//

body.translated_text: If <s>vaktra</s> (narrator), <s>aparavaktra</s> (secondary narrator), and the presence of <s>ucchvāsas</s> (chapters)

children.text: bhedaś ca dṛṣṭo lambhādir ucchvāso vastu kiṃ tataḥ // DKd_1.27 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>ucchvāsa</s>, beginning with the attainment [of the goal], is a structural matter — what [difference] then? //<s>DKd</s> 1.27//

body.translated_text: Just as with <s>āryā</s> and other [metres], why should there not be entry of <s>vaktra</s> and <s>aparavaktra</s>?

children.text: atraivāntarbhaviṣyanti śeṣāś cākhyānajātayaḥ // DKd_1.28 //
children.translated_text: and the remaining varieties of narrative will be included within this very [category]. //<s>DKd</s> 1.28//

body.translated_text: Therefore, <s>kathā</s> and <s>ākhyāyikā</s> are a single genre designated by two names;

children.text: sargabandhasamā eva naite vaiśeṣikā guṇāḥ // DKd_1.29 //
children.translated_text: these are essentially the same as in <s>sargabandha</s>; they are not distinguishing features [of prose]. //<s>DKd</s> 1.29//

body.translated_text: The abduction of a maiden, battles, separations, triumphs, and so forth —

children.text: mukham iṣṭāsrthasaṃsiddhau kiṃ hi na syāt kṛtātmanām // DKd_1.30 //
children.translated_text: what indeed cannot serve as the opening for the accomplished when they aim at the desired goal? //<s>DKd</s> 1.30//

body.translated_text: A mark invented by a poet is not faulty even [when found] elsewhere;

children.text: gadyapadyamayī kā cic campūr ity abhidhīyate // DKd_1.31 //
children.translated_text: a [work] consisting of both prose and verse is called <s>campū</s>. //<s>DKd</s> 1.31//

body.translated_text: Drama (<s>nāṭaka</s>) and the like are mixed [compositions]; their detailed treatment is elsewhere;

body.text: tad etad vāṅmayaṃ bhūyaḥ saṃskṛtaṃ prākṛtaṃ tathā &

children.text: apabhraṃśāś ca miśraṃ cety āhur āryāś caturvidhaṃ // DKd_1.32 //
children.translated_text: <s>Apabhraṃśa</s>, and mixed — so say the learned. //<s>DKd</s> 1.32//

body.translated_text: This entire realm of literature is again fourfold: <s>Saṃskṛta</s> (Sanskrit), <s>Prākṛta</s>,

body.text: saṃskṛtaṃ nāma daivī vāg anvākhyātā maharṣibhiḥ &

children.text: tadbhavas tatsamo deśīty anekaḥ prākṛtakramaḥ // DKd_1.33 //
children.translated_text: derived from it (<s>tadbhava</s>), resembling it (<s>tatsama</s>), and regional (<s>deśī</s>) — such are the many types of <s>Prākṛta</s>. //<s>DKd</s> 1.33//

body.translated_text: Sanskrit is called the divine speech, as expounded by the great sages;

children.text: sāgaraḥ sūktiratnānāṃ setubandhādi yanmayaṃ // DKd_1.34 //
children.translated_text: [it is] the ocean of jewels of fine speech — the <s>Setubandha</s> and other [works] are composed in it. //<s>DKd</s> 1.34//

body.translated_text: The <s>Mahārāṣṭrī</s> dialect is regarded as the preeminent <s>Prākṛta</s>;

body.text: śaurasenī ca gauḍī ca lāṭī cānyā ca tādṛśī &

children.text: yāti prākṛtam ity evaṃ vyavahāreṣu saṃnidhim // DKd_1.35 //
children.translated_text: attain recognition in usage under the designation '<s>Prākṛta</s>.' //<s>DKd</s> 1.35//

body.translated_text: <s>Śaurasenī</s>, <s>Gauḍī</s>, <s>Lāṭī</s>, and others of that kind

children.text: śāstreṣu saṃskṛtād anyad apabhraṃśatayoditam // DKd_1.36 //
children.translated_text: in the treatises, anything other than Sanskrit is declared as <s>Apabhraṃśa</s>. //<s>DKd</s> 1.36//

body.translated_text: The speech of the <s>Ābhīras</s> and others is regarded in poetry as <s>Apabhraṃśa</s>;

children.text: osarādir apabhraṃśo nāṭakādi tu miśrakam // DKd_1.37 //
children.translated_text: <s>Apabhraṃśa</s>, of <s>osara</s> and the like; and drama (<s>nāṭaka</s>) and the like are mixed. //<s>DKd</s> 1.37//

body.translated_text: Sanskrit [takes the form of] <s>sargabandha</s> and the like; <s>Prākṛta</s>, of <s>skandhaka</s> and the like;

body.text: kathā hi sarvabhāṣābhiḥ saṃskṛtena ca badhyate &

children.text: bhūtabhāṣāmayīṃ prāhur adbhutārthāṃ bṛhatkathām // DKd_1.38 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Bṛhatkathā</s>, composed in <s>Bhūtabhāṣā</s> (the language of spirits, i.e. <s>Paiśācī</s>), is said to have marvellous content. //<s>DKd</s> 1.38//

body.translated_text: A story, indeed, is composed in all languages, including Sanskrit;

children.text: śravyam eveti saiṣāpi dvayī gatir udāhṛtā // DKd_1.39 //
children.translated_text: is for hearing alone — thus this twofold classification has been stated. //<s>DKd</s> 1.39//

body.translated_text: Dance, gesture, lightning-displays, and the like are for viewing; the rest, however,

body.text: asty aneko girāṃ mārgaḥ sūkṣmabhedaḥ parasparam &

children.text: tatra vaidarbhagauḍīyau varṇyete prasphuṭāntarau // DKd_1.40 //
children.translated_text: among them, the <s>Vaidarbha</s> and <s>Gauḍīya</s> [styles] are described, being clearly distinct. //<s>DKd</s> 1.40//

body.translated_text: There are many paths of speech, with subtle differences from one another;

children.text: arthavyaktir udāratvam ojaḥkāntisamādhayaḥ // DKd_1.41 //
children.translated_text: <s>arthavyakti</s> (clarity of meaning), <s>udāratva</s> (sublimity), <s>ojas</s> (vigor), <s>kānti</s> (charm), and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration); //<s>DKd</s> 1.41//

body.translated_text: <s>Śleṣa</s> (cohesion), <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity), <s>samatā</s> (evenness), <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness), <s>sukumāratā</s> (delicacy),

body.text: iti vaidarbhamārgasya prāṇā daśa guṇāḥ smṛtāḥ &

children.text: eṣāṃ viparyayaḥ prāyo dṛśyate gauḍavartmani // DKd_1.42 //
children.translated_text: the opposite of these is generally seen in the <s>Gauḍa</s> path. //<s>DKd</s> 1.42//

body.translated_text: thus, the ten qualities are known as the life-breath of the <s>Vaidarbha</s> style;

children.text: śithilaṃ mālatīmālā lolālikalilā yathā // DKd_1.43 //
children.translated_text: flowing — like a garland of <s>mālatī</s> flowers [visited by] a swaying series of bees; //<s>DKd</s> 1.43//

body.translated_text: That which is cohesive (<s>śliṣṭa</s>), untouched by looseness, with few aspirated consonants and more vowels,

children.text: vaidarbhamālatīdāma laṅghitaṃ bhramarair iti // DKd_1.44 //
children.translated_text: [they say:] 'The <s>Vaidarbha</s> garland of <s>mālatī</s> has been surpassed by the bees!' //<s>DKd</s> 1.44//

body.translated_text: that is favored by the <s>Gauḍas</s> on account of its alliterative quality and the weight of its construction —

children.text: lakṣma lakṣmīṃ tanotīti pratītisubhagaṃ vacaḥ // DKd_1.45 //
children.translated_text: by its mark extends [further] beauty' — such speech is pleasing through easy comprehension. //<s>DKd</s> 1.45//

body.translated_text: That which has lucidity, conveying well-known meaning — 'The moon, having the radiance of a blue lotus,

children.text: yathānatyarjunābjanmasadṛkṣāṅko valakṣaguḥ // DKd_1.46 //
children.translated_text: as in: 'The white-rayed [moon], not entirely white, having a mark resembling a lotus not born from [<s>Arjuna</s>].' //<s>DKd</s> 1.46//

body.translated_text: But by the <s>Gauḍīyas</s>, even what is not widely current is desired [if it is] learned —

children.text: bandhā mṛdusphuṭonmiśravarṇavinyāsayonayaḥ // DKd_1.47 //
children.translated_text: the [types of] composition are born from the arrangement of syllables that are soft, clear, or mixed. //<s>DKd</s> 1.47//

body.translated_text: Even in compositions — that which is not uneven, being soft, clear, and moderate;

children.text: ucchalacchīkarācchācchanirjharāmbhaḥkaṇokṣitaḥ // DKd_1.48 //
children.translated_text: sprinkled with drops of water from cascading waterfalls with leaping sprays;' //<s>DKd</s> 1.48//

body.translated_text: 'The <s>Malaya</s> breeze, chattering with the songs of cuckoos, comes to me,

children.text: spardhate ruddhamaddhairyo vararāmāmukhānilaiḥ // DKd_1.49 //
children.translated_text: with restrained boldness, competes with the breeze from the faces of beautiful women;' //<s>DKd</s> 1.49//

body.translated_text: 'The gentle <s>Malaya</s> breeze, fragrant with the passion of sandalwood,

children.text: avekṣamāṇā vavṛdhe paurastyā kāvyapaddhatiḥ // DKd_1.50 //
children.translated_text: the eastern school of poetry grew. //<s>DKd</s> 1.50//

body.translated_text: thus, without considering unevenness, [and merely] regarding sense-ornaments as impressive,

body.text: madhuraṃ rasavad vāci vastuny api rasasthitiḥ &

children.text: yena mādyanti dhīmanto madhuneva madhuvratāḥ // DKd_1.51 //
children.translated_text: by which the wise become intoxicated, like honey-bees by honey. //<s>DKd</s> 1.51//

body.translated_text: Sweet is that which has <s>rasa</s> (flavor) in speech — where <s>rasa</s> resides even in the subject-matter,

body.text: yayā kayā cic chrutyā yat samānam anubhūyate &

children.text: tadrūpā hi padāsattiḥ sānuprāsā rasāvahā // DKd_1.52 //
children.translated_text: that correspondence of words accompanied by alliteration is productive of <s>rasa</s>. //<s>DKd</s> 1.52//

body.translated_text: Whatever is experienced as similar through any [kind of] hearing,

body.text: eṣa rājā yadā lakṣmīṃ prāptavān brāhmaṇapriyaḥ &

children.text: tadā prabhṛti dharmasya loke 'sminn utsavo 'bhavat // DKd_1.53 //
children.translated_text: from that time forth there was a festival of <s>dharma</s> in this world;' //<s>DKd</s> 1.53//

body.translated_text: 'When this king, dear to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, obtained sovereignty,

body.text: itīdaṃ nādṛtaṃ gauḍair anuprāsas tu tatpriyaḥ &

children.text: anuprāsād api prāyo vaidarbhair idam īpsitam // DKd_1.54 //
children.translated_text: yet more than alliteration, this [quality] is desired by the <s>Vaidarbhas</s>. //<s>DKd</s> 1.54//

body.translated_text: this is not favored by the <s>Gauḍas</s>, but alliteration (<s>anuprāsa</s>) is dear to them;

body.text: varṇāvṛttir anuprāsaḥ pādeṣu ca padeṣu ca &

children.text: pūrvānubhavasaṃskārabodhinī yady adūratā // DKd_1.55 //
children.translated_text: it awakens earlier experience and impressions, provided it is not [repeated from] too far away. //<s>DKd</s> 1.55//

body.translated_text: The repetition of sounds, in verse-feet and in words, is <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration);

children.text: indranīlanibhaṃ lakṣma saṃdadhāty alinaḥ śriyam // DKd_1.56 //
children.translated_text: its mark, resembling a blue sapphire, creates the beauty of the bee.' //<s>DKd</s> 1.56//

body.translated_text: 'On the moon — the crest-jewel of autumn nights, displaying the playful charm of <s>kunda</s>-flower clusters —

body.text: cāru cāndramasaṃ bhīru bimbaṃ paśyaitad ambare &

children.text: manmano manmathākrāntaṃ nirdayaṃ hantum udyataṃ // DKd_1.57 //
children.translated_text: my mind, seized by <s>Manmatha</s> (Love), is mercilessly preparing to kill [me].' //<s>DKd</s> 1.57//

body.translated_text: 'Timid one, behold this beautiful disc of the moon in the sky —

children.text: na tu rāmāmukhāmbhojasadṛśaś candramā iti // DKd_1.58 //
children.translated_text: not, however, 'The moon resembles the lotus-face of the beloved woman.' //<s>DKd</s> 1.58//

body.translated_text: Thus they desire alliteration where the repeated sounds are heard at not too great an interval;

body.text: smaraḥ kharaḥ khalaḥ kāntaḥ kāyaḥ kopaś ca naḥ kṛśaḥ &

children.text: ity anyonyopamā seyam anyonyotkarṣaśaṃsinī // DKd_2.18 //
children.translated_text: this is <s>anyonyopamā</s> (mutual simile), suggesting the excellence of each. // DKd_2.18 //

body.translated_text: Your face is like a lotus, the lotus is like your face —

body.text: tvanmukhaṃ kamalenaiva tulyaṃ nānyena kena cit &

children.text: ity anyasāmyavyāvṛtter iyaṃ sā niyamopamā // DKd_2.19 //
children.translated_text: this, from excluding similarity with anything else, is <s>niyamopamā</s> (exclusive simile). // DKd_2.19 //

body.translated_text: Your face is comparable to the lotus alone, and to nothing else —

body.text: padmaṃ tāvat tavānveti mukham anyac ca tādṛśam &

children.text: asti ced astu tatkārīty asāv aniyamopamā // DKd_2.20 //
children.translated_text: let it be so — that is <s>aniyamopamā</s> (non-exclusive simile). // DKd_2.20 //

body.translated_text: The lotus first matches your face; and if something else also resembles it,

body.text: samuccayopamāpy asti na kāntyaiva mukhaṃ tava &

children.text: hlādanākhyena cānveti karmaṇendum itīdṛśī // DKd_2.21 //
children.translated_text: but also by the quality called 'gladdening' — such is this [type]. // DKd_2.21 //

body.translated_text: There is also <s>samuccayopamā</s> (cumulative simile): your face resembles the moon not by beauty alone

body.text: tvayy eva tvanmukhaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ dṛśyate divi candramāḥ &

children.text: iyaty eva bhidā nānyety asāv atiśayopamā // DKd_2.22 //
children.translated_text: this alone is the difference, nothing else — that is <s>atiśayopamā</s> (simile of superiority). // DKd_2.22 //

body.translated_text: Your face is seen only in you; the moon is seen in the sky —

body.text: mayy evāsyā mukahśrīr ity alam indor vikatthanaiḥ &

children.text: padme 'pi sā yad asty evety asāv utprekṣitopamā // DKd_2.23 //
children.translated_text: it exists in the lotus too — that is <s>utprekṣitopamā</s> (imaginative simile). // DKd_2.23 //

body.translated_text: 'The glory of her face is in me alone' — enough of the moon's boasting;

body.text: yadi kiṃ cid bhavet padmaṃ subhru vibhrāntalocanam &

children.text: tat te mukhaśriyaṃ dhattām ity asāv adbhutopamā // DKd_2.24 //
children.translated_text: then it would bear the beauty of your face — that is <s>adbhutopamā</s> (wondrous simile). // DKd_2.24 //

body.translated_text: If the lotus could somehow be fair-browed and rolling-eyed,

children.text: indum apy anudhāvāmīty eṣā mohopamā smṛtā // DKd_2.25 //
children.translated_text: I chase after the moon too — this is called <s>mohopamā</s> (simile of delusion). // DKd_2.25 //

body.translated_text: Fancying your face to be the moon, O slender one, out of desire for your face,

body.text: kiṃ padmam antarbhrāntāli kiṃ te lolekṣaṇaṃ mukham &

children.text: mama dolāyate cittam itīyaṃ saṃśayopamā // DKd_2.26 //
children.translated_text: My mind swings [in doubt] — this is <s>saṃśayopamā</s> (simile of doubt). // DKd_2.26 //

body.translated_text: Is it a lotus with a bee wandering within? Or is it your face with rolling eyes?

children.text: atas tvanmukham evedam ity asau nirṇayopamā // DKd_2.27 //
children.translated_text: therefore this must be your very face — that is <s>nirṇayopamā</s> (simile of determination). // DKd_2.27 //

body.translated_text: The lotus does not have the brilliance to eclipse the moon or to shame it;

children.text: ambhojam iva te vaktram iti śleṣopamā smṛtā // DKd_2.28 //
children.translated_text: your face is like a lotus — this is called <s>śleṣopamā</s> (simile with double meaning). // DKd_2.28 //

body.translated_text: Rivaling the cool-rayed [moon], beautiful, and fragrant —

children.text: bālevodyānamāleyaṃ sālakānanaśobhinī // DKd_2.29 //
children.translated_text: 'This garland of gardens, adorned with <s>sāla</s> trees and forest groves.' // DKd_2.29 //

body.translated_text: That is <s>samānopamā</s> (homonymous simile), from being expressed by words of similar form, as:

body.text: padmaṃ bahurajaś candraḥ kṣayī tābhyāṃ tavānanam &

children.text: samānam api sotsekam iti nindopamā smṛtā // DKd_2.30 //
children.translated_text: though equal to them, surpasses them — this is called <s>nindopamā</s> (simile of censure). // DKd_2.30 //

body.translated_text: The lotus has much pollen; the moon wanes — your face,

children.text: tau tulyau tvanmukheneti sā praśaṃsopamocyate // DKd_2.31 //
children.translated_text: yet they are merely equal to your face — that is called <s>praśaṃsopamā</s> (simile of praise). // DKd_2.31 //

body.translated_text: The lotus is the birthplace of <s>Brahmā</s>; the moon is borne on <s>Śambhu's</s> head —

body.text: candreṇa tvanmukhaṃ tulyam ity ācikhyāsu me manaḥ &

children.text: sa guṇo vāstu doṣo vety ācikhyāsopamāṃ viduḥ // DKd_2.32 //
children.translated_text: whether that be a virtue or a fault, they call that <s>ācikhyāsopamā</s> (simile of desire to express). // DKd_2.32 //

body.translated_text: My mind wished to say 'Your face is equal to the moon' —

children.text: parasparavirodhīti sā virodhopamā matā // DKd_2.33 //
children.translated_text: are mutually contradictory [as standards] — that is considered <s>virodhopamā</s> (simile of contradiction). // DKd_2.33 //

body.translated_text: The hundred-petaled [lotus], the autumn moon, and your face — these three

body.text: na jātu śaktir indos te mukhena pratigarjitum &

children.text: kalaṅkino jaḍasyeti pratiṣedhopamaiva sā // DKd_2.34 //
children.translated_text: being blemished and inert — that is indeed <s>pratiṣedhopamā</s> (simile of negation). // DKd_2.34 //

body.translated_text: The moon can never roar back at your face,

children.text: tathāpi sama evāsau notkarṣīti caṭūpamā // DKd_2.35 //
children.translated_text: yet even so, it is only equal, not superior — that is <s>caṭūpamā</s> (flattering simile). // DKd_2.35 //

body.translated_text: Your face is marked with deer-eyed [beauty]; the moon too is marked with a deer;

body.text: na padmaṃ mukham evedaṃ na bhṛṅgau cakṣuṣī ime &

children.text: iti vispaṣṭasādṛśyāt tattvākhyānopamaiva sā // DKd_2.36 //
children.translated_text: from such manifest resemblance, that is <s>tattvākhyānopamā</s> (simile of truth-telling). // DKd_2.36 //

body.translated_text: This is not a lotus — it is your very face; these are not bees but your eyes —

children.text: ātmanaivābhavat tulyam ity asādhāraṇopamā // DKd_2.37 //
children.translated_text: became comparable only to itself — that is <s>asādhāraṇopamā</s> (incomparable simile). // DKd_2.37 //

body.translated_text: Your face, having surpassed the beauty of the moon and the lotus,

children.text: tvadānanaṃ vibhātīti tām abhūtopamāṃ viduḥ // DKd_2.38 //
children.translated_text: were gathered together in one place — they call that <s>abhūtopamā</s> (impossible simile). // DKd_2.38 //

body.translated_text: Your face shines as if the entire essence of all lotuses' beauty

body.text: candrabimbād iva viṣaṃ candanād iva pāvakaḥ &

children.text: paruṣā vāg ito vaktrād ity asaṃbhāvitopamā // DKd_2.39 //
children.translated_text: [so] harsh speech from this mouth — that is <s>asaṃbhāvitopamā</s> (inconceivable simile). // DKd_2.39 //

body.translated_text: As poison from the moon-orb, as fire from sandalwood —

children.text: sparśas tavety atiśayaṃ bodhayanti bahūpamā // DKd_2.40 //
children.translated_text: your touch indicates excellence through many [comparisons] — that is <s>bahūpamā</s> (multiple simile). // DKd_2.40 //

body.translated_text: Cool like sandalwood-water, moonbeams, moonstone, and the like —

children.text: tava tanvaṅgi vadanam ity asau vikriyopamā // DKd_2.41 //
children.translated_text: as if extracted from the heart of a lotus — that is <s>vikriyopamā</s> (simile of transformation). // DKd_2.41 //

body.translated_text: Your face, O slender one, is as if carved from the moon-orb,

children.text: vikramas tvayy adhāl lakṣmīm iti mālopamā matā // DKd_2.42 //
children.translated_text: so valor bestowed beauty upon you — that is considered <s>mālopamā</s> (garland simile). // DKd_2.42 //

body.translated_text: As heat [belongs to] the sun, as the sun to the day, as daylight to the sky,

children.text: ekānekevaśabdatvāt sā vākyārthopamā dvidhā // DKd_2.43 //
children.translated_text: being of two kinds according to having one or more comparative words — that is <s>vākyārthopamā</s> (simile of sentence meaning), twofold: // DKd_2.43 //

body.translated_text: When one sentence-meaning is compared with another sentence-meaning,

children.text: bhramadbhṛṅgam ivālakṣyakesaraṃ bhāti paṅkajam // DKd_2.44 //
children.translated_text: shines like a lotus with barely visible stamens and wandering bees. // DKd_2.44 //

body.translated_text: Your face, with restless eyes, revealing the splendor of teeth,

body.text: nalinyā iva tanvaṅgyās tasyāḥ padmam ivānanam &

children.text: mayā madhuvrateneva pāyaṃ pāyam aramyata // DKd_2.45 //
children.translated_text: as by a honeybee, so by me — I delighted [in her] again and again. // DKd_2.45 //

body.translated_text: As with a lotus pond, so with that slender-limbed woman; as with a lotus, so with her face;

children.text: sāmyapratītir astīti prativastūpamā yathā // DKd_2.46 //
children.translated_text: the cognition of similarity arises — that is <s>prativastūpamā</s> (counterpart simile), as: // DKd_2.46 //

body.translated_text: When, having presented some object, and then placing something sharing its quality,

children.text: nanu dvitīyo nāsty eva pārijātasya pādapaḥ // DKd_2.47 //
children.translated_text: indeed there is no second tree of the <s>Pārijāta</s>. // DKd_2.47 //

body.translated_text: Not a single one like you, O king, has been born among kings even today;

children.text: yad bruvanti smṛtā seyaṃ tulyayogopamā yathā // DKd_2.48 //
children.translated_text: and spoken of — this is known as <s>tulyayogopamā</s> (simile of equal action), as: // DKd_2.48 //

body.translated_text: When a superior and an inferior are equated in a single action

body.text: divo jagarti rakṣāyai pulomārir bhuvo bhavān &

children.text: asurās tena hanyante sāvalepās tvayā nṛpāḥ // DKd_2.49 //
children.translated_text: by him the demons are slain, and by you the arrogant kings. // DKd_2.49 //

body.translated_text: <s>Pulomāri</s> (<s>Indra</s>) watches over heaven for its protection, and you over the earth;

body.text: kāntyā candramasaṃ dhāmnā sūryaṃ dhairyeṇa cārṇavam &

children.text: rājann anukaroṣīti saiṣā hetūpamā matā // DKd_2.50 //
children.translated_text: that is considered <s>hetūpamā</s> (causal simile). // DKd_2.50 //

body.translated_text: O king, you imitate the moon in beauty, the sun in radiance, and the ocean in steadfastness —

body.text: na liṅgavacane bhinne na hīnādhikatāpi vā &

children.text: upamādūṣaṇāyālaṃ yatrodvego na dhīmatām // DKd_2.51 //
children.translated_text: is not enough to constitute a flaw in simile, where the wise feel no discomfort. // DKd_2.51 //

body.translated_text: A difference in gender or number [between the standard and subject]

body.text: strīva gacchati ṣaṇḍho 'yaṃ vakty eṣā strī pumān iva &

children.text: prāṇā iva priyo 'yaṃ me vidyā dhanam ivārjitā // DKd_2.52 //
children.translated_text: 'this [friend] is dear to me like my very life-breaths'; 'learning has been acquired like wealth.' // DKd_2.52 //

body.translated_text: 'This eunuch walks like a woman'; 'this woman speaks like a man';

children.text: alam aṃśumataḥ kakṣām āroḍhuṃ tejasā nṛpah // DKd_2.53 //
children.translated_text: 'the king has radiance enough to ascend to the level of the sun.' // DKd_2.53 //

body.translated_text: 'O king, the lord of the gods shines like you' —

body.text: ityevamādau saubhāgyaṃ na jahāty eva jātu cit &

children.text: asty eva kva cid udvegaḥ prayoge vāgvidāṃ yathā // DKd_2.54 //
children.translated_text: but there is indeed discomfort in some usages, as among experts in speech, for example: // DKd_2.54 //

body.translated_text: In such and similar cases, [the simile] never loses its charm;

children.text: bhartṛbhakto bhaṭaḥ śveva khadyoto bhāti bhānuvat // DKd_2.55 //
children.translated_text: 'a soldier loyal to his master is like a dog'; 'a firefly shines like the sun.' // DKd_2.55 //

body.translated_text: 'The moon is white like a goose'; 'the sky is clear like a lake';

body.text: īdṛśaṃ varjyate sadbhiḥ kāraṇaṃ tatra cintyatāṃ &

children.text: guṇadoṣavicārāya svayam eva manīṣibhiḥ // DKd_2.56 //
children.translated_text: for the discrimination of merits and faults, by the intelligent themselves. // DKd_2.56 //

body.translated_text: Such [similes] are avoided by the wise; let the reason be considered

children.text: tulyasaṃkāśanīkāśaprakāśapratirūpakāḥ // DKd_2.57 //
children.translated_text: <s>tulya</s>, <s>saṃkāśa</s>, <s>nīkāśa</s>, <s>prakāśa</s>, <s>pratirūpaka</s>; // DKd_2.57 //

body.translated_text: <s>Iva</s>, <s>vat</s>, <s>vā</s>, <s>yathā</s>; <s>samāna</s>, <s>nibha</s>, <s>saṃnibha</s>;

children.text: sadṛksadṛśasaṃvādisajātīyānuvādinaḥ // DKd_2.58 //
children.translated_text: <s>sadṛś</s>, <s>sadṛśa</s>, <s>saṃvādin</s>, <s>sajātīya</s>, <s>anuvādin</s>; // DKd_2.58 //

body.translated_text: <s>pratipakṣa</s>, <s>pratidvandvin</s>, <s>pratyanīka</s>, <s>virodhin</s>;

children.text: salakṣaṇasadṛkṣābhasapakṣopamitopamāḥ // DKd_2.59 //
children.translated_text: <s>salakṣaṇa</s>, <s>sadṛkṣa</s>, <s>ābha</s>, <s>sapakṣa</s>, <s>upamita</s>, <s>upamā</s>; // DKd_2.59 //

body.translated_text: <s>pratibimba</s>, <s>praticchanda</s>, <s>sarūpa</s>, <s>sama</s>, <s>saṃmita</s>;

children.text: savarṇatulitau śabdau ye cānyūnārthavādinaḥ // DKd_2.60 //
children.translated_text: <s>savarṇa</s>, <s>tulita</s> — and whatever other words convey the same meaning; // DKd_2.60 //

body.translated_text: <s>kalpa</s>, <s>deśīya</s>, <s>deśya</s>, etc.; <s>prakhya</s>, <s>pratinidhi</s>;

children.text: spardhate jayati dveṣṭi druhyati pratigarjati // DKd_2.61 //
children.translated_text: 'competes with,' 'conquers,' 'hates,' 'harms,' 'thunders against,' // DKd_2.61 //

body.translated_text: also the <s>bahuvrīhi</s> compound, as in 'moon-faced' and the like; [and verbs such as:]

children.text: viḍambayati saṃdhatte hasatīrṣyaty asūyati // DKd_2.62 //
children.translated_text: 'mimics,' 'challenges,' 'laughs at,' 'envies,' 'begrudges,' // DKd_2.62 //

body.translated_text: 'reviles,' 'disdains,' 'disregards,' 'censures,'

body.text: tasya muṣṇāti saubhāgyaṃ tasya kāntiṃ vilumpati &

children.text: tena sārdhaṃ vigṛhṇāti tulāṃ tenādhirohati // DKd_2.63 //
children.translated_text: 'quarrels with him,' 'ascends his scale,' // DKd_2.63 //

body.translated_text: 'steals his beauty,' 'plunders her radiance,'

body.text: tatpadavyāṃ padaṃ dhatte tasya kakṣāṃ vigāhate &

children.text: tam anvety anubadhnāti tacchīlaṃ tan niṣedhati // DKd_2.64 //
children.translated_text: 'follows him,' 'binds to him,' 'imitates his nature,' 'forbids him.' // DKd_2.64 //

body.translated_text: 'treads in his footsteps,' 'enters his domain,'

body.text:
tasya cānukarotīti śabdāḥ sādṛśyasūcakāḥ &
 upamāyām ime proktāḥ kavīnāṃ buddhisaukhyadāḥ //ity upamācakram// // DKd_2.65 //
body.translated_text: And [the word] 'anukaroti' (imitates it) — such words are indicators of similarity; these are declared in <s>upamā</s> (simile), giving delight to the intellects of poets. //Thus the wheel of <s>upamā</s>.// // DKd 2.65 //

children.text: yathā bāhulatā pāṇipadmaṃ caraṇapallavaḥ // DKd_2.66 //
children.translated_text: For example: 'arm-creeper' (<s>bāhulatā</s>), 'hand-lotus' (<s>pāṇipadma</s>), 'foot-sprout' (<s>caraṇapallava</s>) // DKd 2.66 //

body.translated_text: <s>Upamā</s> (simile) itself with concealed distinction is called <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor);

children.text: bāhū late vasantaśrīs tvaṃ naḥ pratyakṣacāriṇī // DKd_2.67 //
children.translated_text: The two arms were creepers — you, O spring-beauty, walk before us as a living presence // DKd 2.67 //

body.translated_text: The fingers were tendrils, the nail-rays were flowers;

children.text: smitaṃ mukhendor jyotsneti samastavyastarūpakam // DKd_2.68 //
children.translated_text: 'The moonlight of the smile of the face-moon' — this is the compounded-and-non-compounded (<s>samastavyasta</s>) <s>rūpaka</s> // DKd 2.68 //

body.translated_text: This is the non-compounded (<s>asamasta</s>) [<s>rūpaka</s>], and the former is the compounded (<s>samasta</s>) <s>rūpaka</s>;

children.text: dhriyate mūrdhni bhūpālair bhavaccaraṇapaṅkajam // DKd_2.69 //
children.translated_text: Your foot-lotus is borne on the heads of kings // DKd 2.69 //

body.translated_text: With rows of petals that are crimson fingers, with filaments that are nail-rays,

children.text: tadyogyasthānavinyāsād etat sakalarūpakam // DKd_2.70 //
children.translated_text: Through placement [of each attribute] in its fitting position — this is <s>sakala-rūpaka</s> (complete metaphor) // DKd 2.70 //

body.translated_text: Attributing petal-ness etc. to the fingers etc. and lotus-ness to the foot,

children.text: mukhaṃ muktāruco dhatte dharmāmbhaḥkaṇamañjarīḥ // DKd_2.71 //
children.translated_text: Bears clusters of dharma-water-drops with the luster of pearls // DKd 2.71 //

body.translated_text: Suddenly, O fierce one, your face, with its trembling lip-sprout,

children.text: nānyathā kṛtam atrāsyam ato 'vayavarūpakam // DKd_2.72 //
children.translated_text: But the face is not otherwise altered — therefore [this is] <s>avayava-rūpaka</s> (part-metaphor) // DKd 2.72 //

body.translated_text: Making the dharma-water into clusters and the lip into a sprout,

children.text: vivṛṇoti madāvasthām idaṃ vadanapaṅkajam // DKd_2.73 //
children.translated_text: This face-lotus reveals the state of intoxication // DKd 2.73 //

body.translated_text: With trembling eyebrows, dripping dharma-water, with reddish eyes,

children.text: āsīd gamitam atredam ato 'vayavirūpakam // DKd_2.74 //
children.translated_text: Here this was thus done — therefore [this is] <s>avayavi-rūpaka</s> (whole-metaphor) // DKd 2.74 //

body.translated_text: Without altering the parts of the face, the face itself was made into a lotus;

children.text: mukhena mugdhaḥ so 'py eṣa jano rāgamayaḥ krtaḥ // DKd_2.75 //
children.translated_text: By your face, even that bewildered person is made entirely colored with passion // DKd 2.75 //

body.translated_text: With a cheek flushed by intoxication, with eyes like red lotuses,

children.text: aṅgāni rūpayanty atra yogāyogau bhidākarau // DKd_2.76 //
children.translated_text: The limbs create metaphor here — conjunction and disjunction create the distinction // DKd 2.76 //

body.translated_text: This is one-limb (<s>ekāṅga</s>) <s>rūpaka</s>; similarly for two [limbs] and more;

children.text: iti puṣpadvirephāṇāṃ saṃgatyā yuktarūpakam // DKd_2.77 //
children.translated_text: Thus, through the conjunction of flowers and bees, [this is] <s>yukta-rūpaka</s> (conjoined metaphor) // DKd 2.77 //

body.translated_text: This face, bright with smile-flowers, with restless eye-bees —

children.text: iti jyotsnotpalāyogād ayuktaṃ nāma rūpakam // DKd_2.78 //
children.translated_text: Thus, through the disjunction of moonlight and lotuses, [this is] <s>ayukta-rūpaka</s> (disjoined metaphor) // DKd 2.78 //

body.translated_text: This face, with moonlight of moist smiles and lotuses of tender eyes —

children.text: rūpakaṃ viṣamaṃ nāma lalitaṃ jāyate yathā // DKd_2.79 //
children.translated_text: A <s>rūpaka</s> called <s>viṣama</s> (uneven) arises, [which is also] <s>lalita</s> (graceful), as follows: // DKd 2.79 //

body.translated_text: From the metaphorizing of the whole (<s>aṅgin</s>) and its parts (<s>aṅgas</s>), and from the basis of metaphorizing and non-metaphorizing,

children.text: nartitabhrūlatenālaṃ mardituṃ bhuvanatrayam // DKd_2.80 //
children.translated_text: With dancing eyebrow-creepers — <s>Manmatha</s> (Kāma) is well able to crush the three worlds // DKd 2.80 //

body.translated_text: With your face-moon having a cheek reddened by passion,

children.text: jayaty asuraniḥśaṅkasurānandotsavadhvajaḥ // DKd_2.81 //
children.translated_text: He triumphs — the banner of fearlessness for gods and the joy-festival against demons // DKd 2.81 //

body.translated_text: He whose feet are <s>Hari</s>'s, whose head-garment is the water of the daughter of <s>Jahnu</s> (<s>Gaṅgā</s>),
