children.translated_text: You speak of departure! By me, that [your wish] is desired // DKd 2.149 //

body.translated_text: You who are angry at the blinking of the eyelids for the momentary obstruction of seeing —

children.text: tayā niṣidhyate yātrānyasyārthasopasūcanat // DKd_2.150 //
children.translated_text: the journey is forbidden, with a hint of another purpose. [DKd 2.150]

body.translated_text: This is the <s>ākṣepa</s> (reproach) of being under another's control, wherein by her who is subject to love,

body.text: sahiṣye virahaṃ nātha dehy adṛśyāñjanaṃ mama &

children.text: yad aktanetrāṃ kandarpaḥ prahartā māṃ na paśyati // DKd_2.151 //
children.translated_text: so that when my eyes are anointed, <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love), the striker, will not see me." [DKd 2.151]

body.translated_text: "I shall endure the separation, O lord; give me the ointment of invisibility,

children.text: patyuḥ prasthānam ity āhur upāyākṣepam īdṛśam // DKd_2.152 //
children.translated_text: of the husband's setting forth — this is called <s>upāyākṣepa</s> (reproach through a stratagem) of this kind. [DKd 2.152]

body.translated_text: A difficult means of survival is proposed, and thereby the departure is obstructed;

body.text: pravṛttaiva prayāmīti vāṇī vallabha te mukhāt &

children.text: ayatāpi tvayedānīṃ mandapremṇā mamāsti kim // DKd_2.153 //
children.translated_text: even unsought by you, now with your feeble love, what use is it to me?" [DKd 2.153]

body.translated_text: "The word 'I shall go' has indeed issued, O beloved, from your mouth;

children.text: saṃrabdhayā priyārabdhaṃ prayāṇaṃ yan niṣidhyate // DKd_2.154 //
children.translated_text: who in her agitation forbids the journey undertaken by her beloved. [DKd 2.154]

body.translated_text: This is <s>roṣākṣepa</s> (reproach through anger), by her whose self is restrained by overflowing affection,

children.text: buddhvā vakti priyaṃ dṛṣṭvā kiṃ cireṇāgato bhavān // DKd_2.155 //
children.translated_text: upon awakening, seeing her beloved, she says: 'Why have you come after so long?' [DKd 2.155]

body.translated_text: A naive woman, merely upon hearing her beloved's mention of a journey, falls into a swoon;

children.text: kāntasya kātarākṣyā yan mūrchākṣepa sa īdṛśaḥ // DKd_2.156 //
children.translated_text: of the beloved, by her whose eyes are anxious — such is <s>mūrchākṣepa</s> (reproach through swooning) of this kind. [DKd 2.156]

body.translated_text: Thus the departure is reproached through the swoon arising at that very moment;

body.text: nāghrātaṃ na kṛtaṃ karṇe strībhir madhuni nārpitam &

children.text: tvaddviṣāṃ dīrghikāsyeva viśīrṇaṃ nīlam utpalam // DKd_2.157 //
children.translated_text: the blue lotus from the pool of your enemies has simply withered away." [DKd 2.157]

body.translated_text: "It was not smelled, not placed upon the ear, by women; nor was it offered to honey —

children.text: vyāvartya karma tadyogyaṃ śocyāvasthopadarśanāt // DKd_2.158 //
children.translated_text: by diverting action appropriate to it, through the display of a pitiable condition. [DKd 2.158]

body.translated_text: This is <s>anukrośākṣepa</s> (reproach through compassion), as if showing compassion toward the lotus,

children.text: mukhendau tava satyasminn apareṇa kim indunā // DKd_2.159 //
children.translated_text: with tender stars — what need is there of another moon?" [DKd 2.159]

body.translated_text: "When your face-moon exists — of nectar-essence, hating lotuses,

children.text: tatsamān darśayitveha śliṣṭākṣepas tathāvidhaḥ // DKd_2.160 //
children.translated_text: are shown to be equal to it here — such is <s>śliṣṭākṣepa</s> (reproach through double meaning) of that kind. [DKd 2.160]

body.translated_text: Thus the primary moon is reproached; the qualities residing in the secondary moon

body.text: artho na saṃbhṛtaḥ kaś cin na vidyā kā cid arcitā &

children.text: na tapaḥ saṃcintaṃ kiṃ cid gataṃ ca sakalaṃ vayaḥ // DKd_2.161 //
children.translated_text: no austerity whatsoever has been practiced, and the entire lifespan has passed." [DKd 2.161]

body.translated_text: "No wealth whatsoever has been accumulated, no learning whatsoever has been honored,

children.text: arthārjanāder vyāvṛttir darśiteha gatāyuṣā // DKd_2.162 //
children.translated_text: the turning away from wealth-earning and the like is shown here by one whose life has passed. [DKd 2.162]

body.translated_text: This is <s>anuśayākṣepa</s> (reproach through regret), because following regret,

body.text: kim ayaṃ śaradambhodaḥ kiṃ vā haṃsakadambakam &

children.text: rutaṃ nūpurasaṃvādi śrūyate tan na toyadaḥ // DKd_2.163 //
children.translated_text: A sound concordant with anklets is heard — so it is not a cloud." [DKd 2.163]

body.translated_text: "Is this an autumn cloud, or is it a flock of swans?

body.text: ity ayaṃ saṃśayākṣepaḥ saṃśayo yan nivartyate &

children.text: dharmeṇa haṃsasulabhenāspṛṣṭaghanajānitā // DKd_2.164 //
children.translated_text: through a property natural to swans — the knowledge that it is untouched by clouds. [DKd 2.164]

body.translated_text: This is <s>saṃśayākṣepa</s> (reproach through doubt), wherein the doubt is resolved

body.text: citram ākrāntaviśvo 'pi vikramas te na tṛpyati &

children.text: kadā vā dṛśyate tṛptir udīrṇasya havir bhujaḥ // DKd_2.165 //
children.translated_text: But when is satisfaction ever seen in a blazing fire that consumes oblations?" [DKd 2.165]

body.translated_text: "How wondrous! Though you have conquered the entire world, your valor is not satisfied.

children.text: vismayo 'rthantarasyeha darśanāt tatsadharmaṇaḥ // DKd_2.166 //
children.translated_text: the wonder here arises from showing another matter that shares the same nature. [DKd 2.166]

body.translated_text: This is <s>arthāntarākṣepa</s> (reproach through another matter), wherein the ongoing topic is checked;

body.text: na stūyase narendra tvaṃ dadāsīti kadā cana &

children.text: svam eva matvā gṛhṇanti yatas tvad dhanam arthinaḥ // DKd_2.167 //
children.translated_text: for supplicants take your wealth considering it their own." [DKd 2.167]

body.translated_text: "You are never praised, O king, with the words 'you give';

body.text:
ityevamādir ākṣepo hetvākṣepa iti smṛtaḥ &
anenaiva diśānye 'pi vikalpāḥ śakyam ūhitum // ity ākṣepacakram// // DKd_2.168 //
body.translated_text: This and similar types constitute <s>hetvākṣepa</s> (reproach through reasoning), it is held; by this same direction other variations too can be inferred. [Thus ends the <s>ākṣepa</s> cycle.] [DKd 2.168]

body.text: jñeyah so 'rthāntaranyāso vastu prastutya kiṃ cana &

children.text: tatsādhanasamarthasya nyāso yo 'nyasya vastunaḥ // DKd_2.169 //
children.translated_text: the introduction of another matter that is capable of establishing it. [DKd 2.169]

body.translated_text: That is to be known as <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration by another matter): having introduced some subject,

children.text: ayuktakārī yuktātmā yuktāyukto viparyayaḥ // DKd_2.170 //
children.translated_text: doing what is improper yet being appropriate, appropriate-and-inappropriate, and the reverse — [DKd 2.170]

body.translated_text: Universal, particular, interwoven with <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning), containing contradiction,

children.text: udāharaṇamālaiṣāṃ rūpavyaktyai nidarśyate // DKd_2.171 //
children.translated_text: a garland of examples for these is displayed to clarify their forms. [DKd 2.171]

body.translated_text: these and other varieties of it are observed in usage;

children.text: paśya gacchata evāstaṃ niyatiḥ kena laṅghyate // DKd_2.172 //
children.translated_text: behold, they too go to their setting. By whom can destiny be transgressed?" [DKd 2.172]

body.translated_text: "The two blessed eyes of the world, <s>Sūrya</s> (the sun) and <s>Candra</s> (the moon) also —

children.text: nav ātmalābho mahatāṃ paraduḥkhopaśāntaye // DKd_2.173 //
children.translated_text: is not the self-attainment of the great for the alleviation of others' sorrow?" [DKd 2.173]

body.translated_text: "Rain clouds indeed remove the suffering of embodied beings;

children.text: nanu dākṣiṇyasaṃpannaḥ sarvasya bhavati priyaḥ // DKd_2.174 //
children.translated_text: indeed, one endowed with graciousness becomes dear to all." [DKd 2.174]

body.translated_text: "The <s>Malaya</s> breeze produces delight in the world;

children.text: anugṛhṇāti hi parān sadoṣo 'pi dvijeśvaraḥ // DKd_2.175 //
children.translated_text: indeed, a lord among the twice-born bestows grace upon others even though possessing faults." [DKd 2.175]

body.translated_text: "This moon delights the world even though it is blemished;

children.text: kaṭur bhavati karṇasya kāmināṃ pāpam īdṛśam // DKd_2.176 //
children.translated_text: becomes harsh to the ears of lovers — such is the sin of passion." [DKd 2.176]

body.translated_text: "The hum of bees, though issuing from throats engaged in the art of drinking honey,

children.text: hutāśanapratinidhir dāhātmā nanu yujyate // DKd_2.177 //
children.translated_text: is it not fitting that a substitute for fire should have a burning nature?" [DKd 2.177]

body.translated_text: "This bed of lotus petals burns my body;

body.text: kṣiṇotu kāmaṃ śītāṃśuḥ kiṃ vasanto dunoti mām &

children.text: malinācaritaṃ karma surabher nanv asāṃpratam // DKd_2.178 //
children.translated_text: Indeed, the conduct of the gentle breeze is improper and untimely." [DKd 2.178]

body.translated_text: "Let the cool-rayed moon consume me as it pleases — but why does the spring torment me?

body.text:
kumudāny api dāhāya kim ayaṃ kamalākaraḥ &
na hīndugṛhyeṣūgreṣu sūryagṛhyo madhur bhavet //ity arthāntaranyāsacakram// // DKd_2.179 //
body.translated_text: "Are even the night-lotuses for burning? What then of this lotus pond? Surely one sheltered by the moon's family would not be sweet among the fierce ones sheltered by the sun's family." [Thus ends the <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> cycle.] [DKd 2.179]

body.text: śabdopātte prātīte vā sādṛśye vastunor dvayoḥ &

children.text: tatra yad bhedakathanaṃ vyatirekaḥ sa kathyate // DKd_2.180 //
children.translated_text: the statement of difference therein — that is called <s>vyatireka</s> (distinction). [DKd 2.180]

body.translated_text: When there is similarity between two objects, either stated verbally or implied,

children.text: guṇais tulyo 'si bhedas tu vapuṣaivedṛśena te // DKd_2.181 //
children.translated_text: the difference, however, lies only in your body being of this kind." [DKd 2.181]

body.translated_text: "In steadfastness, beauty, depth, and other qualities you are equal to the ocean;

children.text: pratītiviṣayaprāpter bhedasyobhayavartinaḥ // DKd_2.182 //
children.translated_text: because the difference, which exists in both, has reached the domain of implication. [DKd 2.182]

body.translated_text: This is <s>ekavyatireka</s> (single distinction), through a quality residing in one alone,

children.text: asāv añjanasaṃkāśas tvaṃ tu cāmīkaradyutiḥ // DKd_2.183 //
children.translated_text: that one is collyrium-dark, but you are of golden radiance." [DKd 2.183]

body.translated_text: "The ocean and you are both of unsurpassed depth and immeasurable;

children.text: kārṣṇyaṃ piśaṅgatā cobhau yat pṛthag darśitāv iha // DKd_2.184 //
children.translated_text: — darkness and golden hue — are both shown separately here. [DKd 2.184]

body.translated_text: This is <s>ubhayavyatireka</s> (double distinction), where two distinguishing qualities

body.text: tvaṃ samudraś ca durvārau mahāsattvau satejasau &

children.text: ayaṃ tu yuvayor bhedaḥ sa jaḍātmā paṭur bhavān // DKd_2.185 //
children.translated_text: but this is the difference between you two: he is insentient, while you are brilliant." [DKd 2.185]

body.translated_text: "You and the ocean are both irresistible, of great essence, and possessed of splendor;

body.text: sa eṣa śleṣarūpatvāt saśleṣa iti gṛhyatām &

children.text: sākṣepaś ca sahetuś ca darśyate tad api dvayam // DKd_2.186 //
children.translated_text: the varieties 'with reproach' and 'with reason' are also demonstrated — that pair as well. [DKd 2.186]

body.translated_text: That very same, because it has the form of <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning), should be understood as <s>saśleṣa</s> (with double meaning);

body.text: sthitimān api dhīro 'pi ratnānām ākaro 'pi san &

children.text: tava kakṣāṃ na yāty eva malino makarālayaḥ // DKd_2.187 //
children.translated_text: the impure abode of sea-monsters never attains your rank." [DKd 2.187]

body.translated_text: "Though possessed of steadfastness, though resolute, though being a mine of gems,

children.text: bhartṛbhāvād bhujaṅgānāṃ śeṣas tvatto nikṛṣyate // DKd_2.188 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śeṣa</s> is diminished compared to you, because of being a lord of serpents." [DKd 2.188]

body.translated_text: "Though bearing the entire earth with its mountains, continents, and oceans,

children.text: pratīyamānasādṛśyo 'py asti so 'py abhidhīyate // DKd_2.189 //
children.translated_text: there is also one based on implied similarity — that too is described. [DKd 2.189]

body.translated_text: This is <s>vyatireka</s> (distinction) based on verbally stated similarity, of this kind;

body.text: tvanmukhaṃ kamalaṃ ceti dvayor apy anayor bhidā &

children.text: kamalaṃ jalasaṃrohi tvanmukhaṃ tvadupāśrayam // DKd_2.190 //
children.translated_text: the lotus grows in water, while your face is in your care." [DKd 2.190]

body.translated_text: "Your face and a lotus — between these two the difference is:

children.text: idaṃ tu nayanadvandvaṃ tava taguṇabhūṣitam // DKd_2.191 //
children.translated_text: yet this pair of eyes of yours is adorned with those very qualities." [DKd 2.191]

body.translated_text: "Without the play of eyebrows, untouched by the flush of passion, deer-eyed —

children.text: sadṛśavyatirekaś ca punar anyaḥ pradarśyate // DKd_2.192 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>vyatireka</s> (distinction) of similars is further demonstrated as yet another type. [DKd 2.192]

body.translated_text: In the former, mere statement of difference; in this one, the showing of superiority;

children.text: bhramadbhramaram ambhojaṃ lolanetraṃ mukhaṃ tu te // DKd_2.193 //
children.translated_text: the lotus has a hovering bee, while your face has a roving eye." [DKd 2.193]

body.translated_text: "Your face and the white lotus — when in bloom, both are sweet-scented;

children.text: nabho nakṣatramālīdam utphullakumudaṃ payaḥ // DKd_2.194 //
children.translated_text: this sky has a garland of stars; this water has fully blossomed night-lotuses." [DKd 2.194]

body.translated_text: "This moon is the crest-jewel of the sky; this swan is the ornament of water;

children.text: kṛtaḥ pratītaśuddhyoś ca bhedo 'smiṃś candrahaṃsayoḥ // DKd_2.195 //
children.translated_text: the distinction is made in this verse between the moon and the swan, whose purity is also implied. [DKd 2.195]

body.translated_text: Of the sky and water, whose similarity in whiteness and the like is implied,

children.text: bhṛṅganetrādi tulyaṃ tat sadṛśavyatirekatā // DKd_2.196 //
children.translated_text: — the bee and the eye, etc. — is equal; that constitutes the <s>sadṛśavyatireka</s> (distinction of similars). [DKd 2.196]

body.translated_text: In the former, the similarity is as if verbally stated; in both, the distinguishing element

children.text: dṛṣṭirodhakaraṃ yūnāṃ yauvanaprabhavaṃ tamaḥ // DKd_2.197 //
children.translated_text: obstructing the sight of young men — this is the darkness born of youth." [DKd 2.197]

body.translated_text: "Removable by the light of a mere forearm's length, not removable by the sun's rays,

body.text:
sajātīvyatireko 'yaṃ tamojāter idaṃ tamaḥ &
dṛṣṭirodhitayā tulyaṃ bhinnam anyair adarśi tat //iti vyatirekacakram// // DKd_2.198 //
body.translated_text: This is <s>sajātīyavyatireka</s> (distinction within the same class): this darkness, being of the class of darkness, is equal in obstructing sight, but is shown as different in other respects. [Thus ends the <s>vyatireka</s> cycle.] [DKd 2.198]

children.text: yatra svābhāvikatvaṃ vā vibhāvyaṃ sā vibhāvanā // DKd_2.199 //
children.translated_text: or naturalness itself is to be suggested — that is <s>vibhāvanā</s> (poetic fancy). [DKd 2.199]

body.translated_text: Where, by the exclusion of the well-known cause, some other cause

children.text: aprasāditaśuddhāmbu jagad āsīn manoharam // DKd_2.200 //
children.translated_text: without the pure waters having been clarified — the world was enchanting." [DKd 2.200]

body.translated_text: "Without parrots having drunk <s>kṣība</s> (intoxicating liquor), without the forehead of the sky having been wiped clean,

children.text: arañjito 'ruṇaś cāyam adharas tava sundari // DKd_2.201 //
children.translated_text: un-reddened yet crimson is this lip of yours, O beautiful one." [DKd 2.201]

body.translated_text: "Un-anointed yet dark is your gaze; un-bent yet curved is your brow;

children.text: ahetukaṃ ca tasyeha vivakṣety aviruddhatā // DKd_2.202 //
children.translated_text: and what is without cause — the intention of expressing that here is not contradictory. [DKd 2.202]

body.translated_text: What would be produced by drinking etc., what would have another cause such as intoxication,

children.text: akāraṇaripuś candro nirnimittāsuhṛt smaraḥ // DKd_2.203 //
children.translated_text: the moon is an enemy without cause; <s>Smara</s> (the god of love) is a foe without reason." [DKd 2.203]

body.translated_text: "The face is naturally fragrant; the body is beautiful without artifice;

body.text:
nisargādipadair atra hetuḥ sākṣān nivartitaḥ &
uktaṃ ca surabhitvādi phalaṃ tat sā vibhāvanā //iti vibhāvanācakram// // DKd_2.204 //
body.translated_text: Here, through words like 'naturally' etc., the cause is directly negated, and the effect such as fragrance is stated — that is <s>vibhāvanā</s> (poetic fancy). [Thus ends the <s>vibhāvanā</s> cycle.] [DKd 2.204]

children.text: uktiḥ saṃkṣeparūpatvāt sā samāsoktir iṣyate // DKd_2.205 //
children.translated_text: because it has the nature of condensed expression — that is regarded as <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression). [DKd 2.205]

body.translated_text: Having intended a certain object, the description of another object similar to it,

children.text: apy asaṃnaddhasaurabhyaṃ paśya cumbati kuḍmalam // DKd_2.206 //
children.translated_text: the bee — see! — kisses even the bud that has not yet released its fragrance." [DKd 2.206]

body.translated_text: "Drinking honey as he pleases from a fully blossomed lotus,

children.text: kasyāṃ cid iha bālāyām icchāvṛttir vibhāvyate // DKd_2.207 //
children.translated_text: the desire-driven conduct toward some young girl is suggested here. [DKd 2.207]

body.translated_text: Thus, of a passionate man whose amorous play is that of a mature woman,

children.text: asty asāv aparāpy asti bhinnābhinnaviśeṣaṇā // DKd_2.208 //
children.translated_text: there exists that type; and there is also another with different and non-different qualifiers. [DKd 2.208]

body.translated_text: Even when differing only in the qualified object, having the same form of qualifier,

children.text: sāndracchāyo mahāvṛkṣaḥ so 'yam āsādito mayā // DKd_2.209 //
children.translated_text: a great tree of dense shade — he has been reached by me." [DKd 2.209]

body.translated_text: "With roots firmly established, nourishing supplicants constantly with the burden of his fruits,

children.text: socchrayaḥ sthairyavān daivād eṣa labdho mayā drumaḥ // DKd_2.210 //
children.translated_text: lofty, possessed of firmness — by fortune this tree has been obtained by me." [DKd 2.210]

body.translated_text: "Of no small expanse of branches, abundant in fruits and flowers,

children.text: sarve sādhāraṇā dharmāḥ pūrvatrānyatra tu dvayam // DKd_2.211 //
children.translated_text: all the qualities are shared in the former; but in the latter, two are distinct. [DKd 2.211]

body.translated_text: In both cases a certain man is described under the guise of a tree;

children.text: ayam ambhonidhiḥ kaṣṭaṃ kālena pariśuṣyati // DKd_2.212 //
children.translated_text: this ocean, alas, is drying up with time." [DKd 2.212]

body.translated_text: "Free from association with serpents, naturally sweet in disposition —

body.text:
ity āpūrvasamāsoktiḥ pūrvadharmanivartanāt &
samudreṇa samānasya puṃso vyāpattisūcanāt //iti samāsokticakram// // DKd_2.213 //
body.translated_text: This is a novel <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression), because of the negation of the former properties; it hints at the calamity of a man who is similar to the ocean. [Thus ends the <s>samāsokti</s> cycle.] [DKd 2.213]

children.text: asāv atiśayoktiḥ syād alaṃkārottamā yathā // DKd_2.214 //
children.translated_text: that is <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole), the foremost of ornaments, as follows: [DKd 2.214]

body.translated_text: The intention to express a particular quality that transcends the limits of the ordinary world —

children.text: kṣaumavatyo na lakṣyante jyotsnāyām abhisārikāḥ // DKd_2.215 //
children.translated_text: clad in fine linen — the <s>abhisārikā</s>s (women going to secret trysts) are not visible in the moonlight." [DKd 2.215]

body.translated_text: "Wearing garlands of <s>mallikā</s> (jasmine), with moist sandalwood paste over their entire bodies,

children.text: saṃśayātiśayādīnāṃ vyaktyai kiṃ cin nidarśyate // DKd_2.216 //
children.translated_text: for the clarification of doubt-based hyperbole and the like, something is illustrated: [DKd 2.216]

body.translated_text: The abundance of moonlight is expressed through exaggeration;

body.text: stanayor jaghanasyāpi madhye madhyaṃ priye tava &

children.text: asti nāstīti saṃdeho na me 'dyāpi nivartate // DKd_2.217 //
children.translated_text: exists or does not exist — that doubt of mine has not been resolved even to this day." [DKd 2.217]

body.translated_text: "Between your breasts and your hips, O beloved, whether your waist

body.text: nirṇetuṃ śakyam astīti madhyaṃ tava nitambini &

children.text: anyathānupapattyaiva payodharabharasthiteḥ // DKd_2.218 //
children.translated_text: only through the impossibility of any other explanation for the stability of the weight of your breasts." [DKd 2.218]

body.translated_text: "It can be determined that your waist does exist, O woman of ample hips,

children.text: māti mātum aśakyo 'pi yaśorāśir yad atra te // DKd_2.219 //
children.translated_text: that your mass of fame, though immeasurable, is contained within it!" [DKd 2.219]

body.translated_text: "O king, how vast is the belly of the three worlds,

body.text:
alaṃkārāntarāṇām apy ekam āhuḥ parāyaṇam &
vāgīśamahitām uktim imām atiśayāhvayam //ity atiśayokticakram// // DKd_2.220 //
body.translated_text: Some call this expression, honored by the lord of speech, the supreme refuge of all other ornaments, by the name <s>atiśaya</s> (hyperbole). [Thus ends the <s>atiśayokti</s> cycle.] [DKd 2.220]

children.text: anyathotprekṣyate yatra tām utprekṣāṃ vidur yathā // DKd_2.221 //
children.translated_text: is imagined to be otherwise — that the learned know as <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy/imaginative identification), as follows: [DKd 2.221]

body.translated_text: Where the actual state of a conscious or non-conscious being

children.text: manye mārtaṇḍagṛhyāṇi padmāny uddhartum udyataḥ // DKd_2.222 //
children.translated_text: I think he is eager to uproot the lotuses that belong to the sun's household." [DKd 2.222]

body.translated_text: "An elephant scorched by the midday sun enters the lake;

body.text: snātuṃ pātuṃ bisāny attuṃ kariṇo jalagāhanam &

children.text: tadvairaniṣkrayāyeti kavinotprekṣya varṇyate // DKd_2.223 //
children.translated_text: is described by the poet as being imagined to be for avenging the enmity with the sun. [DKd 2.223]

body.translated_text: The elephant's entering the water to bathe, to drink, and to eat lotus stalks

children.text: iti karṇotpalaṃ prāyas tava dṛṣṭyā vilaṅghyate // DKd_2.224 //
children.translated_text: is mostly overstepped by your sidelong glance." [DKd 2.224]

body.translated_text: "'This is an ornament for my ear' — so thinking, this lotus of the ear of my adversary

children.text: spṛśyate vā na vety evaṃ kavinotprekṣya varṇyate // DKd_2.225 //
children.translated_text: touch the lotus or not — thus the poet describes it through poetic fancy. [DKd 2.225]

body.translated_text: Whether the rays of the sidelong glance falling at the corner of the eye

children.text: itīdam api bhūyiṣṭham utprekṣālakṣaṇānanvitam // DKd_2.226 //
children.translated_text: this too is mostly characterized by the marks of <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy). [DKd 2.226]

body.translated_text: "The darkness smears the limbs, as it were; the sky rains collyrium, as it were" —

children.text: nopamānaṃ tiṅantenety atikramyāptabhāṣitam // DKd_2.227 //
children.translated_text: but 'the standard of comparison should not be a finite verb' — thus transgressing the established teaching. [DKd 2.227]

body.translated_text: For some, the confusion with <s>upamā</s> (simile) arises here due to hearing the word 'iva' (as it were);

children.text: limpates tamasaś cāsau dharmaḥ ko 'tra samīkṣyate // DKd_2.228 //
children.translated_text: of the smearing action and of darkness — what shared quality is to be discerned here? [DKd 2.228]

body.translated_text: The status of standard and object of comparison depends on a shared quality;

body.text: yadi lepanam eveṣṭaṃ limpatir nāma ko 'paraḥ &

children.text: sa eva dharmo dharmī cety anunmatto na bhāṣate // DKd_2.229 //
children.translated_text: That the quality and the possessor of the quality are the same — no one not mad would say this. [DKd 2.229]

body.translated_text: If smearing itself is the intended quality, then what other 'smearing' is there?

body.text: kartā yady upamānaṃ syān nyagbhūto 'sau kriyāpade &

children.text: svakriyāsādhanavyagro nālam anyad apekṣitum // DKd_2.230 //
children.translated_text: being occupied with accomplishing its own action, it cannot attend to anything else. [DKd 2.230]

body.translated_text: If the agent were the standard of comparison, it would be subordinated in the verbal form;

body.text: yo limpaty amunā tulyaṃ tama ity api śaṃsataḥ &

children.text: aṅgānīti na saṃbaddhaṃ so 'pi mṛgyaḥ samo guṇaḥ // DKd_2.231 //
children.translated_text: 'the limbs' does not connect — and that equal quality too must be sought. [DKd 2.231]

body.translated_text: Even if one says 'the darkness is like that which smears,'

body.text: yathendur iva te vaktram iti kāntiḥ pratīyate &

children.text: na tathā limpater lepād anyad atra pratīyate // DKd_2.232 //
children.translated_text: not so from the smearing of 'smears' — nothing else is understood here. [DKd 2.232]

body.translated_text: Just as in 'your face is like the moon,' beauty is understood,

children.text: aṅgakarmā ca puṃsaivam utprekṣyata itīṣyatām // DKd_2.233 //
children.translated_text: and [the word denoting] 'bodily action' is thus to be imagined as [applicable] to a masculine [agent] — let this be accepted. //DKd 2.233//

body.translated_text: Thus, this [word] '<s>limpati</s>' (smears), whose agent is darkness, is used for the purpose of close contact;

body.text:
manye śaṅke dhruvaṃ prāyo nūnam ityevamādibhiḥ &
utprekṣā vyajyate śabdair ivaśabdo 'pi tādṛśaḥ // ity utprekṣācakram// // DKd_2.234 //
body.translated_text: 'I think,' 'I suspect,' 'certainly,' 'probably,' 'surely' — by such words <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) is expressed; and the word '<s>iva</s>' (like/as if) is also of this kind. //Thus ends the section on <s>utprekṣā</s>.// //DKd 2.234//

body.text: hetuś ca sūkṣmaleśau ca vācām uttamabhūṣaṇam &

children.text: kārakajñāpakau hetū tau cānekavidhau yathā // DKd_2.235 //
children.translated_text: the causes — the effecting and the indicating [kinds] — are of many types, as follows: //DKd 2.235//

body.translated_text: <s>Hetu</s> (cause) and <s>sūkṣma</s> (subtlety) and <s>leśa</s> (hint) are the supreme ornaments of speech;

children.text: utpādayati sarvasya prītiṃ malayamārutaḥ // DKd_2.236 //
children.translated_text: produces delight in everyone. //DKd 2.236//

body.translated_text: This <s>Malaya</s> breeze, which has swayed the mature shoots of the sandal trees,

children.text: alaṃkāratayoddiṣṭaṃ nivṛttāv api tat samam // DKd_2.237 //
children.translated_text: is designated as an ornament; and that [figure] is the same even in the case of cessation [of something]. //DKd 2.237//

body.translated_text: Here, the augmentation of a form capable of producing delight

children.text: pathikānām abhāvāya pavano 'yam upasthitaḥ // DKd_2.238 //
children.translated_text: this wind has arrived for the destruction of travelers. //DKd 2.238//

body.translated_text: Having shaken the sandalwood forests and having touched the mountain-streams of <s>Malaya</s>,

children.text: virahajvarasaṃbhūtamanojñārocake jane // DKd_2.239 //
children.translated_text: for people in whom the [lack of] the pleasure of appetite has arisen due to the fever of separation. //DKd 2.239//

body.translated_text: For a wind of such nature is indeed sufficient as a means of destruction

body.text: nivartye ca vikārye ca hetutvaṃ tadapekṣayā &

children.text: prāpye tu karmaṇi prāyaḥ kriyāpekṣaiva hetutā // DKd_2.240 //
children.translated_text: but in the case of what is to be achieved as an object [of action], the causal relation mostly depends on the action itself. //DKd 2.240//

body.translated_text: In the cases of what is to be prevented and what is to be modified, the causal relation depends on that [context];

children.text: dattvodāharaṇadvandvaṃ jñāpako varṇayiṣyate // DKd_2.241 //
children.translated_text: having given a pair of examples, the indicating [cause] will now be described. //DKd 2.241//

body.translated_text: The cause of what is to be produced has been shown; for the remaining two [kinds],

children.text: candraḥ pūrṇaś ca kāmena pānthadṛṣṭer viṣaṃ kṛtam // DKd_2.242 //
children.translated_text: and the full moon — all these have been made into poison for the eyes of travelers by <s>Kāma</s> (Love). //DKd 2.242//

body.translated_text: The forests with fresh coral-like [flowers], the ponds with fully-bloomed lotuses,

children.text: bālā bhrūbhaṅgajihmākṣī paśyati sphuritādharā // DKd_2.243 //
children.translated_text: looks at her friend who stands in the place of her beloved, with quivering lips. //DKd 2.243//

body.translated_text: 'I shall honor her' — with this thought, the young woman with her brow furrowed and eyes askance

body.text: gato 'stam arko bhātīndur yānti vāsāya pakṣiṇaḥ &

children.text: itīdam api sādhv eva kālāvasthānivedane // DKd_2.244 //
children.translated_text: this too is beautiful indeed in announcing the condition of [evening] time. //DKd 2.244//

body.translated_text: The sun has set, the moon shines, the birds go to their nests —

children.text: dehoṣmabhiḥ subodhaṃ te sakhi kāmāturaṃ manaḥ // DKd_2.245 //
children.translated_text: which cannot be subdued by moonbeams and cannot be remedied by sandalwood and water. //DKd 2.245//

body.translated_text: O friend, your love-stricken mind is easily known by the heat of your body,

children.text: abhāvahetavaḥ ke cid vyāhriyante manoharāḥ // DKd_2.246 //
children.translated_text: some causes of absence [of something] are also expressed charmingly. //DKd 2.246//

body.translated_text: Thus, the delightful indicating causes should be observed in literary compositions;

children.text: anigraheṇa cākṣāṇāṃjāyate vyasanaṃ nṛṇām // DKd_2.247 //
children.translated_text: and through lack of restraint of the senses — calamity arises for people. //DKd 2.247//

body.translated_text: Through lack of practice in learning, through lack of association with the wise,

children.text: kṣato mohaś cyutā tṛṣṇā kṛtaṃ puṇyāśrame manaḥ // DKd_2.248 //
children.translated_text: delusion is destroyed, craving has fallen away — the mind has been placed in the hermitage of merit. //DKd 2.248//

body.translated_text: The intoxication of love-talk is gone, the fever of youth has subsided,

body.text: vanāny amūni na gṛhāṇy etā nadyo na yoṣitaḥ &

children.text: mṛgā ime na dāyādās tan me nandati mānasam // DKd_2.249 //
children.translated_text: these deer are not heirs — therefore my mind rejoices. //DKd 2.249//

body.translated_text: These forests are not houses, these rivers are not women,

children.text: atas teṣāṃ vivardhante satataṃ sarvasaṃpadaḥ // DKd_2.250 //
children.translated_text: therefore their prosperity constantly increases in every way. //DKd 2.250//

body.translated_text: The deeds of the noble are absolutely not looked upon with suspicion;

children.text: deyaḥ pathikanārīṇāṃ satilaḥ salilāñjaliḥ // DKd_2.251 //
children.translated_text: [therefore] an offering of water mixed with sesame should be given to the wives of travelers [in mourning]. //DKd 2.251//

body.translated_text: The mango blossoms in the garden have not yet sprouted —

children.text: bhāvābhāvasvarūpasya kāryasyotpādanaṃ prati // DKd_2.252 //
children.translated_text: is with respect to the production of an effect whose nature is existence or non-existence. //DKd 2.252//

body.translated_text: Here, the causality of a thing whose form is prior non-existence and the like

children.text: ayuktayuktakāryau cety asaṃkhyāś citrahetavaḥ // DKd_2.253 //
children.translated_text: and those whose effects are incongruent and congruent — thus the varieties of <s>hetu</s> (cause) are innumerable. //DKd 2.253//

body.translated_text: A remote cause, one co-arising [with the effect], one immediately preceding the effect,

children.text: atyantasundarā dṛṣṭās tadudāhṛtayo yathā // DKd_2.254 //
children.translated_text: and are seen to be exceedingly beautiful — as shown in the following examples: //DKd 2.254//

body.translated_text: These [causes], in the paths of literary usage, depend on figurative expression,

children.text: muktaṃ tad anyatas tena so 'py ahaṃ manasi kṣataḥ // DKd_2.255 //
children.translated_text: was aimed at another, but through that, even I have been wounded in the heart. //DKd 2.255//

body.translated_text: O beautiful one, that victorious weapon of <s>Anaṅga</s> (Bodiless Love), called 'your sidelong glance,'

children.text: sahaiva vividhaiḥ puṃsām aṅgajonmādavibhramaiḥ // DKd_2.256 //
children.translated_text: together with various love-born disturbances and agitations in men. //DKd 2.256//

body.translated_text: The youth of women, in which childhood is left behind, appears

children.text: prāg eva hariṇākṣīṇām udīrṇo rāgasāgaraḥ // DKd_2.257 //
children.translated_text: but the ocean of passion in the doe-eyed women has risen even before that. //DKd 2.257//

body.translated_text: The disk of the moon, casting its rays behind, has risen,

children.text: deva tvaccaraṇadvandvarāgabālātapaḥ spṛśan // DKd_2.258 //
children.translated_text: O lord, the early morning sunlight of the redness of your two feet touches [them]. //DKd 2.258//

body.translated_text: Why do the lotus-hands of kings close into buds?

children.text: tvatpādanakhacandrāṇām arciṣaḥ kundanirmalāḥ // DKd_2.259 //
children.translated_text: are able to cause the lotus-hands of kings to close. //DKd 2.259//

body.translated_text: The rays of the moons of your toenails, pure as jasmine,

body.text: iti hetuvikalpānāṃ darśitā gatir īdṛśī // iti hetucakram// &

children.text: iṅgitākāralakṣyo 'rthaḥ saukṣmyāt sūkṣma iti smṛtaḥ // DKd_2.260 //
children.translated_text: That meaning which is to be understood through gestures and appearances is called <s>sūkṣma</s> (subtle) because of its subtlety. //DKd 2.260//

body.translated_text: Thus, such is the demonstrated range of the varieties of <s>hetu</s> (cause). //Thus ends the section on <s>hetu</s>.//

body.text: kadā nau saṃgamo bhāvīty ākīrṇe vaktum akṣamam &

children.text: avetya kāntam abalā līlāpadmaṃ nyamīlayat // DKd_2.261 //
children.translated_text: the young woman, understanding [the thought of] her beloved, playfully closed her lotus[-like hand]. //DKd 2.261//

body.translated_text: Unable to say in the presence of others 'when shall we meet?'

children.text: āśvāsayitum icchantyā priyam aṅgajapīḍitam // DKd_2.262 //
children.translated_text: by her who wishes to reassure her beloved afflicted by love. //DKd 2.262//

body.translated_text: Here, by the closing of the lotus, a nocturnal meeting is suggested

children.text: uddāmarāgataralā chāyā kāpi mukhāmbuje // DKd_2.263 //
children.translated_text: there grew a certain radiance, trembling with unbridled passion. //DKd 2.263//

body.translated_text: During a song-gathering, upon the face-lotus of her who had cast her gaze at me,

body.text:
ity anudbhinnarūpatvād ratyutsavamanorathah &
anullaṅhgyaiva sūkṣmatvam abhūd atra vyavasthitaḥ //iti sūkṣmacakram// // DKd_2.264 //
body.translated_text: Thus, because the desire for a festival of love was in a form not yet manifest, the subtlety was absolutely not transgressed — it remained established here. //Thus ends the section on <s>sūkṣma</s>.// //DKd 2.264//

children.text: udāharaṇa evāsya rūpam āvirbhaviṣyati // DKd_2.265 //
children.translated_text: its form will become clear in the following example: //DKd 2.265//

body.translated_text: <s>Leśa</s> (hint) is the concealment of the nature of a thing, broken open by a [mere] trace;

children.text: avagaccheyur ā jñātam aho śītānilaṃ vanam // DKd_2.266 //
children.translated_text: 'ah, the forest has a cold wind!' [he said, to conceal it]. //DKd 2.266//

body.translated_text: The guards might perceive from my horripilation that I am in love with the king's daughter —

body.text: ānandāśru pravṛttaṃ me kathaṃ dṛṣṭvaiva kanyakām &

children.text: akṣi me puṣparajasā vātoddhūtena dūṣitam // DKd_2.267 //
children.translated_text: 'My eye has been irritated by flower-pollen blown up by the wind.' //DKd 2.267//

body.translated_text: How have tears of joy arisen upon merely seeing the maiden?

children.text: leśam eke vidur nindāṃ stutiṃ vā leśataḥ kṛtām // DKd_2.268 //
children.translated_text: some understand <s>leśa</s> as blame or praise done [merely] in a trace. //DKd 2.268//

body.translated_text: Thus, in such situations this ornament is most resplendent;

body.text: yuvaiṣa guṇavān rājā yogyas te patir ūrjitaḥ &

children.text: raṇotsave manaḥ saktaṃ yasya kāmotsavād api // DKd_2.269 //
children.translated_text: his mind is more attached to the festival of battle than to the festival of love.' //DKd 2.269//

body.translated_text: 'This young king is virtuous; he is a worthy and vigorous husband for you;

children.text: kanyāyāḥ kalpate bhogān nirvivikṣor nirantaram // DKd_2.270 //
children.translated_text: the maiden who has no desire for pleasures, from [accepting] one who is constantly [absorbed in war]. //DKd 2.270//

body.translated_text: This praise of the excellence of valor is actually a reproach, intended to dissuade

body.text: capalo nirdayaś cāsau janaḥ kiṃ tena me sakhi &

children.text: āgaḥpramārjanāyaiva cāṭavo yena śikṣitāḥ // DKd_2.271 //
children.translated_text: He in whom sweet talk has been practiced only for the purpose of wiping away offenses.' //DKd 2.271//

body.translated_text: 'That person is fickle and merciless — what is he to me, O friend?

body.text:
doṣābhāso guṇaḥ ko 'pi darśitaś cāṭukāritā &
mānaṃ sakhijanoddiṣṭaṃ kartuṃ rāgād aśaktayā // iti leśacakram// // DKd_2.272 //
body.translated_text: Here, what appears to be a fault is actually some virtue — the art of flattery is shown, and pride declared before friends, by one who is unable to maintain her anger because of love. //Thus ends the section on <s>leśa</s>.// //DKd 2.272//

children.text: yathāsaṃkhyam iti proktaṃ saṃkhyānaṃ krama ity api // DKd_2.273 //
children.translated_text: is called <s>yathāsaṃkhya</s> (enumeration in order), also known as <s>saṃkhyāna</s> (counting) or <s>krama</s> (sequence). //DKd 2.273//

body.translated_text: The mention of stated things in order, one by one,

body.text:
dhruvaṃ te coritā tanvi smitekṣaṇamukhadyutiḥ &
snātum ambhaḥpraviṣṭāyāḥ kumudotpalapaṅkajaiḥ // iti kramaḥ// // DKd_2.274 //
body.translated_text: Surely, O slender one, when you entered the water to bathe, your radiance of smiling, glance, and face was stolen by the water-lilies, blue lotuses, and [red] lotuses [respectively]. //Thus ends [the section on] <s>krama</s>.// //DKd 2.274//

children.text: ūrjasvi rūḍhāhaṃkāraṃ yuktotkarṣaṃ ca tat trayam // DKd_2.275 //
children.translated_text: <s>ūrjasvi</s> (the energetic) has well-established self-assertion and fitting exaltation — these three [are described]. //DKd 2.275//

body.translated_text: <s>Preyas</s> (the delightful) is the narration dearer than the dear; <s>rasavat</s> (having sentiment) is one rich and skillful in <s>rasa</s>;

body.text: adya yā mama govinda jātā tvayi gṛhāgate &

children.text: kālenaiṣā bhavet prītis tavaivāgamanāt punaḥ // DKd_2.276 //
children.translated_text: this love will come to me again in time, only through your return.' //DKd 2.276//

body.translated_text: 'The joy that has arisen in me today, O <s>Govinda</s>, upon your coming home —

body.text: ity āha yuktaṃ viduro nānyatas tādṛśī dhṛtiḥ &

children.text: bhaktimātrasamārādhyaḥ suprītaś ca tato hariḥ // DKd_2.277 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Hari</s>, who is pleased by devotion alone, was greatly delighted. //DKd 2.277//

body.translated_text: Thus spoke <s>Vidura</s> fittingly — from no other source comes such steadfastness;

body.text: somaḥ sūryo marudbhūmir vyoma hotānalo jalam &

children.text: iti rūpāṇy atikramya tvāṃ draṣṭuṃ deva ke vayam // DKd_2.278 //
children.translated_text: having transcended these forms, O Lord, who are we to behold you?' //DKd 2.278//

body.translated_text: '<s>Soma</s> (Moon), <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun), <s>Marut</s> (Wind), <s>Bhūmi</s> (Earth), <s>Vyoma</s> (Sky), <s>Hotṛ</s> (Sacrificer), <s>Anala</s> (Fire), <s>Jala</s> (Water) —

body.text: iti sākṣātkṛte deve rājño yad rātavarmaṇaḥ &

children.text: prītiprakāśanaṃ tac ca preya ity avagamyatām // DKd_2.279 //
children.translated_text: upon directly beholding the deity — let this be understood as <s>preyas</s> (the delightful). //DKd 2.279//

body.translated_text: This expression of delight by King <s>Rātavarman</s>

body.text: mṛte 'ti pretya saṃgantuṃ yayā me maraṇaṃ matam &

children.text: saivāvantī mayā labdhā katham atraiva janmani // DKd_2.280 //
children.translated_text: that very <s>Avantī</s> maiden has been obtained by me in this very life!' //DKd 2.280//

body.translated_text: 'She for whose sake, having died and gone beyond, I thought of dying again to meet her —

body.text: prāk prītir darśitā seyaṃ ratiḥ śṛṅgāratāṃ gatā &

children.text: rūpabāhulyayogena tad idaṃ rasavadvacaḥ // DKd_2.281 //
children.translated_text: by the abundance of its form — that is <s>rasavat</s> (having sentiment) speech. //DKd 2.281//

body.translated_text: Previously, delight was shown; this same love, having reached the state of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment),

body.text: nigṛhya keśeṣv ākṛṣṭā kṛṣṇā yenāgrato mama &

children.text: so 'yaṃ duḥśāsanaḥ pāpo labdhaḥ kiṃ jīvati kṣaṇam // DKd_2.282 //
children.translated_text: that wicked <s>Duḥśāsana</s> has been caught — does he live even a moment?' //DKd 2.282//

body.translated_text: 'He who seized <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> (<s>Draupadī</s>) by the hair and dragged her before me —

body.text: ity āruhya parāṃ koṭiṃ krodho raudrātmatāṃ gataḥ &

children.text: bhīmasya paśyataḥ śatrum ity etad rasavadvacaḥ // DKd_2.283 //
children.translated_text: of <s>Bhīma</s> beholding his enemy — this is <s>rasavat</s> speech. //DKd 2.283//

body.translated_text: Thus, having reached the extreme peak, the anger has attained the nature of the terrifying (<s>raudra</s>) [sentiment],

body.text: ajitvā sārṇavām urvīm aniṣṭvā vividhair makhaiḥ &

children.text: adatvā cārtham arthibhyo bhaveyaḥ pārthivaḥ katham // DKd_2.284 //
children.translated_text: and without giving wealth to suppliants — how could one be a king?' //DKd 2.284//

body.translated_text: 'Without conquering the earth bounded by the ocean, without sacrificing with various sacrifices,

children.text: rasavattvaṃ girām āsāṃ samarthayitum īśvaraḥ // DKd_2.285 //
children.translated_text: is capable of establishing the quality of <s>rasavat</s> (having sentiment) in these words. //DKd 2.285//

body.translated_text: Thus, this exalted determination, standing in the nature of the heroic sentiment (<s>vīra rasa</s>),

children.text: sādhiśete kathaṃ tanvī hutāśanavatīṃ citām // DKd_2.286 //
children.translated_text: how can that slender one now lie upon a funeral pyre full of fire?' //DKd 2.286//

body.translated_text: 'She whose tender body found even a bed of flowers painful —

children.text: tathāpare 'pi bībhatsahāsyādbhutabhayānakāḥ // DKd_2.287 //
children.translated_text: similarly, the other [sentiments] too — the disgusting, the comic, the wondrous, and the terrible. //DKd 2.287//

body.translated_text: Thus, intensified compassion (<s>kāruṇya</s>) is considered as an ornament;

children.text: kauṇapāḥ saha nṛtyanti kabandhair antrabhūṣaṇāḥ // DKd_2.288 //
children.translated_text: the ghouls dance together with headless trunks, adorned with entrails. //DKd 2.288//

body.translated_text: Drinking, drinking the blood of your enemies from cupped hands,

children.text: chādyatām uttarīyeṇa navaṃ nakhapadaṃ sakhi // DKd_2.289 //
children.translated_text: is a fresh nail-mark, O friend — cover it with your upper garment!' //DKd 2.289//

body.translated_text: 'This, on the slope of your breast that remains unfaded with pride,

children.text: śākhāś ca mandirāṇy eṣāṃ citraṃ nandanaśākhinām // DKd_2.290 //
children.translated_text: and branches — these are the houses of these wonderful <s>Nandana</s> (celestial garden) trees!' //DKd 2.290//

body.translated_text: 'Garments, coral, flowers, necklace-ornaments,

children.text: smaraṇaṃ yasya daityastrīgarbhapātāya kalpate // DKd_2.291 //
children.translated_text: the very remembrance of which causes miscarriage in the wives of <s>Daitya</s>s (demons).' //DKd 2.291//

body.translated_text: 'This is the thunderbolt of <s>Maghon</s> (<s>Indra</s>), with fire held ready in its blade,

body.text:
vākyasyāgrāmyatāyonir mādhurye darśito rasaḥ &
iha tv aṣṭarasāyattā rasavattā smṛtā girām //iti rasavaccakram// // DKd_2.292 //
body.translated_text: <s>Rasa</s> (sentiment) has been shown as the source of non-vulgarity and sweetness of speech; but here, the quality of <s>rasavat</s> in speech is considered to depend on all eight <s>rasa</s>s. //Thus ends the section on <s>rasavat</s>.// //DKd 2.292//

body.text: apakartāham asmīti hṛdi te mā sma bhūd bhayam &

children.text: vimukheṣu na me khaḍgaḥ prahartuṃ jātu vāñchati // DKd_2.293 //
children.translated_text: my sword never desires to strike those who have turned their backs [in flight].' //DKd 2.293//

body.translated_text: 'Let there be no fear in your heart that I am one who injures;

body.text:
iti muktaḥ paro yuddhe niruddho darpaśalinā &
puṃsā kenāpi taj jñeyam ūrjasvītyevamādikam //ity ūrjasvi// // DKd_2.294 //
body.translated_text: Thus, one who was released in battle by an opponent possessed of pride after being captured — know this and the like as <s>ūrjasvi</s> (the energetic). //Thus ends [the section on] <s>ūrjasvi</s>.// //DKd 2.294//

body.text: artham iṣṭam anākhyāya sākṣāt tasyaiva siddhaye &

children.text: yat prakārāntarākhyānaṃ paryāyoktaṃ tad iṣyate // DKd_2.295 //
children.translated_text: for the very accomplishment of that [meaning] is regarded as <s>paryāyokta</s> (periphrasis). //DKd 2.295//

body.translated_text: Without directly stating the desired meaning, that which narrates through another manner

children.text: tam ahaṃ vārayiṣyāmi yuvābhyāṃ svairam āsyatām // DKd_2.296 //
children.translated_text: I shall go and drive it away — you two may remain at ease.' //DKd 2.296//

body.translated_text: 'That cuckoo is pecking at the blossom of the mango tree;

body.text:
saṃgamayya sakhīṃ yūnā saṃkete tadratotsavaṃ &
nirvartayitum icchantyā kayāpy apasṛtaṃ tataḥ //iti paryāyoktam// // DKd_2.297 //
body.translated_text: Having brought her friend together with the young man at the rendezvous, wishing to enable their festival of love, she [the go-between] thus withdrew from that place. //Thus ends [the section on] <s>paryāyokta</s>.// //DKd 2.297//

children.text: tatsādhanasamāpattir yā tad āhuḥ samāhitam // DKd_2.298 //
children.translated_text: the accomplishment of that very means comes about [on its own] — that they call <s>samāhita</s> (coincidence). //DKd 2.298//

body.translated_text: When one who is about to undertake something finds that, by the force of fate,

body.text:
mānam asyā nirākartuṃ pādayor me patiṣyataḥ &
upakārāya diṣṭyaitad udīrṇaṃ ghanagarjitam // iti samāhitam// // DKd_2.299 //
body.translated_text: 'I was about to fall at her feet to dispel her anger — fortunately, this thundering of clouds has arisen to [serve as] a pretext!' //Thus ends [the section on] <s>samāhita</s>.// //DKd 2.299//

body.text: āśayasya vibhūter vā yan mahatvam anuttamam &

children.text: udāttaṃ nāma taṃ prāhur alaṃkāraṃ manīṣibhiḥ // DKd_2.300 //
children.translated_text: is what the wise call the ornament known as <s>udātta</s> (the sublime). //DKd 2.300//

body.translated_text: That unsurpassed greatness of intention or of magnificence

body.text: guroḥ śasanam atyetuṃ na śaśāka sa rāghavaḥ &

children.text: yo rāvaṇaśiraśchedakāryabhāre 'py aviklavaḥ // DKd_2.301 //
children.translated_text: he who was unperturbed even under the burden of the task of severing the heads of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>. //DKd 2.301//

body.translated_text: That <s>Rāghava</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) was unable to transgress the command of his father —

children.text: jñāto laṅkeśvaraḥ kṛcchrād āñjaneyena tattvataḥ // DKd_2.302 //
children.translated_text: the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) was recognized with difficulty by <s>Āñjaneya</s> (<s>Hanumān</s>) in his true [form]. //DKd 2.302//

body.translated_text: Surrounded by hundreds of reflections transferred onto walls of gems,

body.text:
pūrvatrāśayamāhātmyam atrābhyudayagauravam &
suvyañjitam iti proktaṃ udāttadvayam apy adaḥ // ity udāttam// // DKd_2.303 //
body.translated_text: In the former [example], the greatness of intention is well-expressed; in the latter, the gravity of prosperity — thus this pair of <s>udātta</s> (sublime) [has been demonstrated]. //Thus ends [the section on] <s>udātta</s>.// //DKd 2.303//

children.text: na pañceṣu smaras tasya sahasraṃ patriṇām iti // DKd_2.304 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Kāma</s> (Love) does not have five arrows — he has a thousand missile-bearing [ones].' //DKd 2.304//

body.translated_text: <s>Apahṇuti</s> (concealment/denial) is the showing of another meaning after denying something:

body.text: candanaṃ candrikā mando gandhavāhaś ca dakṣiṇaḥ &

children.text: seyam agnimayī sṛṣṭir mayi śītā parān prati // DKd_2.305 //
children.translated_text: this is a creation made of fire for me, [though] cool for others. //DKd 2.305//

body.translated_text: Sandalwood, moonlight, the gentle and fragrant southern breeze —

children.text: auṣṇyaprakāśanāt tasya seyaṃ viṣayaniḥnutiḥ // DKd_2.306 //
children.translated_text: by the lover — this is concealment of the [true] nature of the object. //DKd 2.306//

body.translated_text: Having acknowledged the coolness [of these things] for others but [declaring] their heat in himself,

children.text: anya evāyam arthātmā viṣaniṣyandidīdhitiḥ // DKd_2.307 //
children.translated_text: but this is quite another thing in reality — [it has] rays dripping with poison. //DKd 2.307//

body.translated_text: The moon, by name, is considered to have nectar-dripping rays;

children.text: uktā smarārtenety eṣā svarūpāpahnutir matā // DKd_2.308 //
children.translated_text: this, spoken by one afflicted by love, is considered <s>svarūpāpahṇuti</s> (denial of essential nature). //DKd 2.308//

body.translated_text: Thus, the moon-ness of the moon itself is denied and another nature [asserted] —

body.text:
upamāpahnutiḥ pūrvam upamāsv eva darśitā &
ity apahnutibhedānāṃ lakṣyo lakṣyeṣu vistaraḥ //ity apahanutiḥ// // DKd_2.309 //
body.translated_text: The denial-of-comparison (<s>upamāpahṇuti</s>) was previously shown under comparisons. Thus, the details of the varieties of <s>apahṇuti</s> (denial) should be observed in [actual] compositions. //Thus ends [the section on] <s>apahṇuti</s>.// //DKd 2.309//

children.text: tad abhinnapadaṃ bhinnapadaprāyam iti dvidhā // DKd_2.310 //
children.translated_text: it is of two kinds: that with undivided words and that consisting mostly of divided words. //DKd 2.310//

body.translated_text: <s>Śliṣṭa</s> (paronomasia) is speech that is well-joined, has multiple meanings, and is unified in a single form;

children.text: rājā harati lokasya hṛdayaṃ mṛdubhiḥ karaiḥ // DKd_2.311 //
children.translated_text: the king captivates the heart of the world with his gentle rays/hands. //DKd 2.311//

body.translated_text: He has risen to the [point of] rising, radiant, with a red disk —

children.text: rājñā pradoṣo mām ittham apriyaṃ kiṃ na bādhate // DKd_2.312 //
children.translated_text: by the king/dusk — does not this evening thus afflict me with what is displeasing? //DKd 2.312//

body.translated_text: Bound by one who dwells on the path of stars and is a receptacle of faults/night,

children.text: prāg eva darśitāḥ śleṣā darśyante ke canāpare // DKd_2.313 //
children.translated_text: have been shown previously; some others will now be shown. //DKd 2.313//

body.translated_text: The <s>śleṣa</s>s (paronomasias) that fall within the domain of comparison, <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), <s>ākṣepa</s> (objection), <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast), and the like

children.text: viruddhakarmā cāsty anyaḥ śleṣo niyamavān api // DKd_2.314 //
children.translated_text: and yet another with contradictory action; [there is] also <s>śleṣa</s> with restriction. //DKd 2.314//

body.translated_text: There is one [<s>śleṣa</s>] with non-distinct action, another with non-contradictory action,

children.text: teṣāṃ nidarśaneṣv eva rūpam āvirbhaviṣyati // DKd_2.315 //
children.translated_text: their form will become clear in the illustrative examples themselves. //DKd 2.315//

body.translated_text: An expression having the form of restriction, negation, non-contradiction, and contradiction —

children.text: dṛśo dūtyaś ca karṣanti kāntābhiḥ preṣitāḥ priyān // DKd_2.316 //
children.translated_text: Glances and messengers, sent by beloved women, attract their lovers.

body.translated_text: Curved, sweet by nature, proclaiming unbridled passion —

children.text: ākarṇyante madakalāh śliṣyante cāsitekṣanāḥ // DKd_2.317 //
children.translated_text: are heard, intoxicating in their melody, and dark-eyed women are embraced.

body.translated_text: Sweet, passion-increasing, soft voices of cuckoos

children.text: tirobhavati dharmāṃśur aṅgajas tu vijṛṃbhate // DKd_2.318 //
children.translated_text: the ray of <s>dharma</s> disappears, while <s>Aṅgaja</s> (<s>Kāmadeva</s>, the Love-God) expands.

body.translated_text: Displaying passion augmented by the influence of wine,

body.text: nistriṃśatvam asāv eva dhanuṣy evāsya vakratā &

children.text: śareṣv eva narendrasya mārgaṇatvaṃ ca vartate // DKd_2.319 //
children.translated_text: and this king's seeking nature exists only in his arrows.

body.translated_text: His sword-nature resides only in his sword, his crookedness only in his bow,

body.text: padmānām eva daṇḍeṣu kaṇṭakas tvayi rakṣati &

children.text: athavā dṛśyate rāgimithunāliṅganeṣv api // DKd_2.320 //
children.translated_text: or rather, they are seen also in the embraces of passionate couples.

body.translated_text: While you protect, thorns exist only on the stems of lotuses —

children.text: dakṣaḥ prajāpatiś cāsīt svāmī śaktidharaś ca saḥ // DKd_2.321 //
children.translated_text: skilled, lord of subjects (or: <s>Prajāpati</s>), a master, and bearer of power (or: wielder of the spear).

body.translated_text: He who bore many bracelets (or: had many slopes, like a mountain), radiant, of certain rise,

body.text:
acyuto 'py avṛṣacchedī rājāpy aviditakṣayaḥ &
devo 'py avibudho jajñe śaṃkaro 'py abhujaṅgavān //iti śleṣacakram// // DKd_2.322 //
body.translated_text: Though unfallen (or: like <s>Acyuta</s>/<s>Viṣṇu</s>), he was not a destroyer of the bull; though a king, his decline was unknown; though a god, he was not unwise; though auspicious (or: like <s>Śaṃkara</s>/<s>Śiva</s>), he was without serpents. Thus ends the cycle of <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia).

children.text: viśeṣadarśanāyaiva sā viśeṣoktir iṣyate // DKd_2.323 //
children.translated_text: for the very purpose of displaying distinction — that is recognized as <s>viśeṣokti</s> (distinction).

body.translated_text: When there is a showing of the absence of qualities, class, action, and the like,

body.text: na kaṭhoraṃ na vā tīkṣṇam āyudhaṃ puṣpadhanvanaḥ &

children.text: tathāpi jitam evāsīd amunā bhuvanatrayam // DKd_2.324 //
children.translated_text: yet even so, the three worlds were conquered by him.

body.translated_text: The weapon of <s>Puṣpadhanvan</s> (the Flower-Bowed One, i.e. <s>Kāmadeva</s>) is neither harsh nor sharp;

children.text: tathāpy eṣā tapobhaṅgaṃ vidhātuṃ vedhaso 'py alam // DKd_2.325 //
children.translated_text: yet she is capable of disrupting the austerities of even <s>Vedhas</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>).

body.translated_text: She is neither a celestial maiden nor born of the <s>Gandharva</s> lineage;

body.text: na baddhā bhrūkuṭir nāpi sphurito daśanacchadaḥ &

children.text: na ca raktābhavad dṛṣṭir jitaṃ ca dviṣatāṃ kulam // DKd_2.326 //
children.translated_text: nor did the gaze become reddened — yet the host of enemies was conquered.

body.translated_text: No frown was knit, nor was the lip quivering,

body.text: na rathā na ca mātaṅgā na hayā na ca pattayaḥ &

children.text: strīṇām apāṅgadṛṣṭyaiva jīyate jagatāṃ trayam // DKd_2.327 //
children.translated_text: by the sidelong glance of women alone are the three worlds conquered.

body.translated_text: Not by chariots, nor elephants, nor horses, nor foot-soldiers —

body.text: ekacakro ratho yantā vikalo viṣamā hayāḥ &

children.text: ākrāmaty eva tejasvī tathāpy arko nabhastalam // DKd_2.328 //
children.translated_text: yet the radiant <s>Arka</s> (Sun) traverses the vault of the sky.

body.translated_text: His chariot has but one wheel, the charioteer is crippled, the horses are uneven;

body.text:
saiṣā hetuviśeṣoktis tejasvīti viśeṣaṇāt &
ayam eva kramo 'nyeṣāṃ bhedānām api kalpane//iti viśeṣokticakram// // DKd_2.329 //
body.translated_text: This is <s>hetu-viśeṣokti</s> (distinction with reason), indicated by the qualifier 'radiant'; this same method applies in the composition of other varieties as well. Thus ends the cycle of <s>viśeṣokti</s>.

children.text: kīrtanaṃ stutinindārthaṃ sā matā tulyayogitā // DKd_2.330 //
children.translated_text: in the quality intended to be expressed — that is considered <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal conjunction).

body.translated_text: When something is praised or censured by equating it with things that excel

body.text: yamaḥ kubero varuṇaḥ sahasrākṣo bhavān api &

children.text: bibhranty ananyaviṣayāṃ lokapāla iti śrutim // DKd_2.331 //
children.translated_text: all bear the exclusive title of '<s>Lokapāla</s>' (World-Protector).

body.translated_text: <s>Yama</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Sahasrākṣa</s> (Thousand-Eyed <s>Indra</s>), and you as well —

body.text:
saṃgatāni mṛgākṣīṇāṃ taḍidvilasitāni ca &
kṣaṇadvayaṃ na tiṣṭhanti ghanārabdhāny api svayam //iti tulyayogitā// // DKd_2.332 //
body.translated_text: The encounters with doe-eyed women and the flashings of lightning — both do not last for even two moments, even when self-initiated amidst the clouds. Thus ends <s>tulyayogitā</s>.

children.text: viśeṣadarśanāyaiva sa virodhaḥ smṛto yathā // DKd_2.333 //
children.translated_text: for the very purpose of displaying distinction — that is known as <s>virodha</s> (contradiction), as follows:

body.translated_text: Where there is a showing of the conjunction of contradictory things,

children.text: kṣīyate ca mayūrāṇāṃ rutam utkrāntasauṣṭhavam // DKd_2.334 //
children.translated_text: while the cry of peacocks, which had surpassed all beauty, diminishes.

body.translated_text: The cooing of royal swans increases, charming in its intoxication,

children.text: rāgeṇa punar ākrāntaṃ jāyate jagatāṃ manaḥ // DKd_2.335 //
children.translated_text: yet the minds of people, seized by passion, become radiant.

body.translated_text: By the rain-season clouds the sky becomes overcast,

children.text: natanābhi vapuḥ strīṇāṃ kaṃ na haraty unnatastanam // DKd_2.336 //
children.translated_text: with a deep navel and high breasts — what man does the body of women not captivate?

body.translated_text: Slender-waisted, broad-hipped, red-lipped, dark-eyed,

children.text: api te rūpam asmākaṃ tanvi tāpāya kalpate // DKd_2.337 //
children.translated_text: even your beauty, O slender one, serves to torment us.

body.translated_text: With arms like lotus stalks, thighs like plantain stems, a face like a lotus, and eyes like water-lilies —

children.text: udaśrayanti pānthānām aspṛśanto 'pi locane // DKd_2.338 //
children.translated_text: bring tears to the eyes of travelers, even without touching them.

body.translated_text: The pollen of mango and <s>campaka</s> flowers, scattered by garden breezes,

children.text: yāti viśvasanīyatvaṃ kasya te kalabhāṣini // DKd_2.339 //
children.translated_text: whose trust does it gain, O sweet-voiced one?

body.translated_text: Though your gaze is devoted to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> (or: black and white), and depends on <s>Karṇa</s> (or: reaches to the ears),

children.text: aprastutapraśaṃsā syād aprakrānteṣu yā stutiḥ // DKd_2.340 //
children.translated_text: <s>Aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant) is praise directed at things not under discussion.

body.translated_text: Thus this ornament is perceived in many forms. Thus ends the cycle of <s>virodha</s>.

children.text: annair ayatnasulabhais tṛṇadarbhāṅkurādibhiḥ // DKd_2.341 //
children.translated_text: on food easily obtained without effort — grass, <s>darbha</s> sprouts, and the like.

body.translated_text: Happily do the deer live in the forests, serving no master,

body.text:
seyam aprastutaivātra mṛgavṛttiḥ praśasyate &
rājānuvartanakleśanirviṇṇena manasvinā //ity aprastutapraśaṃsā// // DKd_2.342 //
body.translated_text: Here the life of deer, which is not the subject at hand, is praised by a wise man disgusted with the misery of serving a king. Thus ends <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s>.

body.text: yadi nindann iva stauti vyājastutir asau smrtā &

children.text: doṣābhāsā guṇā eva labhante hy atra saṃnidhim // DKd_2.343 //
children.translated_text: for herein only apparent faults, which are actually virtues, come together.

body.translated_text: When one praises as if censuring, that is known as <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise);

children.text: tvayā rājñāpi saiveyaṃ jitā mā bhūn madas tava // DKd_2.344 //
children.translated_text: by you too, though merely a king, this same earth has been conquered — let there be no pride in you!

body.translated_text: Even by <s>Rāma</s>, the ascetic-warrior, was this earth conquered;

body.text: puṃsaḥ purāṇād ācchidya śrīs tvayā paribhujyate &

children.text: rājann ikṣākuvaṃśasya kim idaṃ tava yujyate // DKd_2.345 //
children.translated_text: O king of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> dynasty, is this befitting of you?

body.translated_text: Having snatched <s>Śrī</s> (Prosperity) from the Primeval Being (<s>Puruṣa</s>), she is enjoyed by you —

children.text: ahaṅkāraḥ parāṃ koṭim ārohati kutas tava // DKd_2.346 //
children.translated_text: whence does your pride ascend to the highest peak?

body.translated_text: Your wife, the earth, is embraced by serpent-hoods (or: the enjoyments of serpents);

body.text:
iti śleṣānuviddhānām anyeṣāṃ copalakṣyatām &
vyājastutiprakārāṇām aparyantas tu vistaraḥ //iti vyājastutiḥ// // DKd_2.347 //
body.translated_text: Thus, of these and other varieties of <s>vyājastuti</s> interwoven with <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), the elaboration is endless. Thus ends <s>vyājastuti</s>.

children.text: sad asad vā nidarśyeta yadi tat syān nidarśanam // DKd_2.348 //
children.translated_text: whether real or unreal, is illustrated — that is <s>nidarśana</s> (illustration).

body.translated_text: If, through something pertaining to another matter, a result similar to it,

body.text: udayann eṣa savitā padmeṣv arpayati śriyam &

children.text: vibhāvayitum ṛddhīnāṃ phalaṃ suhṛdanugraham // DKd_2.349 //
children.translated_text: to demonstrate that the fruit of prosperity is the benefaction of friends.

body.translated_text: This rising sun bestows beauty upon the lotuses,

body.text:
yāti candrāṃśubhiḥ spṛṣṭā dhvāntarājī parābhavam &
sadyo rājaviruddhānāṃ sūcayantī durantatām //iti nidarśanam// // DKd_2.350 //
body.translated_text: The streak of darkness, touched by moonbeams, meets defeat — instantly indicating the doom of those who oppose the king. Thus ends <s>nidarśana</s>.

children.text: arthānāṃ yo vinimayaḥ parivṛttis tu sā smṛtā // DKd_2.351 //
children.translated_text: that which is an exchange of meanings is known as <s>parivṛtti</s> (exchange).

body.translated_text: <s>Sahoktih</s> (co-statement) is the narration of qualities and actions as coexisting;

body.text: saha dīrghā mama śvāsair imāḥ samprati rātrayaḥ &

children.text: pāṇḍurāś ca mamaivāṅgeḥ saha tāś candrabhūṣaṇāh // DKd_2.352 //
children.translated_text: and pale together with my limbs are those nights, adorned by the moon.

body.translated_text: These nights are long now, together with my sighs;

children.text: patanti ca samaṃ teṣām asubhir malayānilāḥ // DKd_2.353 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>Malaya</s> breezes fall simultaneously with their life-breaths.

body.translated_text: The mango blossom grows together with the travelers' swoon;

children.text: yānti sārdhaṃ janānandair vṛddhiṃ surabhivāsarāḥ // DKd_2.354 //
children.translated_text: the pleasant spring days grow together with the delights of people.

body.translated_text: Lovely with the songs of cuckoos, bearing fragrant forest breezes,

body.text: ity udāhṛtayo dattāḥ sahokter atra kāś cana //iti sahoktiḥ// &

children.text: kriyate parivṛtteś ca kiṃ cid rūpanidarśanam // DKd_2.355 //
children.translated_text: And now a brief illustration of <s>parivṛtti</s> is given.

body.translated_text: Thus some examples of <s>sahoktih</s> have been given here. Thus ends <s>sahoktih</s>.

body.text:
śastraprahāraṃ dadatā bhujena tava bhūbhujām &
cirārjitaṃ hṛtaṃ teṣāṃ yaśaḥ kumudapāṇḍuram //iti parivṛttiḥ// // DKd_2.356 //
body.translated_text: By your arm, which deals blows with weapons to kings, their long-accumulated fame, white as <s>kumuda</s> (night-lotus), has been seized. Thus ends <s>parivṛtti</s>.

body.text:
āśīrnāmābhilaṣite vastuny āśaṃsanaṃ yathā &
pātu vaḥ paramaṃ jyotir avāṅmanasagocaram //ity āśīḥ// // DKd_2.357 //
body.translated_text: <s>Āśīḥ</s> (benediction) is the expression of a wish for a desired thing, as: 'May the supreme light, beyond the reach of speech and mind, protect you.' Thus ends <s>āśīḥ</s>.

children.text: upamārūpakaṃ cāpi rūpakeṣv eva darśitam // DKd_2.358 //
children.translated_text: and <s>upamārūpaka</s> (simile-metaphor) has been shown under <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor).

body.translated_text: <s>Ananvaya</s> (unique comparison) and <s>saṃdeha</s> (doubt) have been shown under <s>upamā</s> (simile);

children.text: nānālaṃkārasaṃsṛṣṭiḥ saṃsṛṣṭis tu nigadyate // DKd_2.359 //
children.translated_text: the combination of various ornaments is called <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination).

body.translated_text: That is indeed a variety of <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), and also a component of <s>utprekṣā</s>;

children.text: ity alaṃkārasaṃsṛṣṭer lakṣaṇīyā dvayī gatiḥ // DKd_2.360 //
children.translated_text: thus in the combination of ornaments, two arrangements are to be recognized.

body.translated_text: The relationship of subordinate and principal, or the equality of all —

children.text: kośadaṇḍasamagrāṇāṃ kim eṣām asti duṣkaram // DKd_2.361 //
children.translated_text: for those equipped with treasury and army (or: calyx and stem), what is difficult?

body.translated_text: The lotuses challenge the beauty of your face, O innocent one;

children.text: asatpuruṣaseveva dṛṣṭir niṣphalatāṃ gatā // DKd_2.362 //
children.translated_text: like the service of a wicked man, sight has become fruitless.

body.translated_text: Darkness seems to smear the limbs, the sky seems to rain collyrium;

body.text:
śleṣaḥ sarvāsu puṣṇāti prāyo vakroktiṣu śriyam &
bhinnaṃ dvidhā svabhāvoktir vakroktiś ceti vāṅmayam //iti saṃsṛṣtiḥ// // DKd_2.363 //
body.translated_text: <s>Śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) nourishes beauty in nearly all <s>vakroktis</s> (indirect expressions); speech is divided twofold: <s>svabhāvokti</s> (natural description) and <s>vakrokti</s> (indirect expression). Thus ends <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s>.

body.text: tad bhāvikam iti prāhuḥ prabandhaviṣayaṃ guṇam &

children.text: bhāvaḥ kaver abhiprāyaḥ kāvyeṣv āsiddhi saṃsthitaḥ // DKd_2.364 //
children.translated_text: <s>bhāva</s> (sentiment) is the poet's intention, established in poetry until its completion.

body.translated_text: They call that quality <s>bhāvika</s> (suggestive), which pertains to the composition as a whole;

children.text: viśeṣāṇāṃ vyarthānām akriyā sthānavarṇanā // DKd_2.365 //
children.translated_text: the avoidance of purposeless particulars, and the description of settings —

body.translated_text: The mutual helpfulness of all narrative junctures,

body.text:
vyaktir uktikramabalād gambhīrasyāpi vastunaḥ &
bhāvāyattām idaṃ sarvam iti tad bhāvikaṃ viduḥ //iti bhāvikam// // DKd_2.366 //
body.translated_text: the manifestation of even a profound subject through the power of sequential expression — all this depends on <s>bhāva</s>; thus they know it as <s>bhāvika</s>. Thus ends <s>bhāvika</s>.

children.text: vyāvarṇitam idaṃ ceṣṭam alaṅkāratayāiva naḥ // DKd_2.367 //
children.translated_text: this has been intended by us as ornaments (<s>alaṅkāra</s>) alone.

body.translated_text: And that which has been described as <s>saṃdhi</s> (juncture), <s>aṅga</s> (element), <s>vṛtti</s> (style), <s>aṅgalakṣaṇa</s> (characteristics of elements), and the like in other treatises —

body.text: panthāḥ sa eṣa vivṛtaḥ parimāṇavṛttyā saṃhṛtya vistaram anantam alaṅkriyāṇām &

children.text: vācām atītya viṣayaṃ parivartamānān abhyāsa eva vivarītum alaṃ viśeṣān // DKd_2.368 //
children.translated_text: the distinctions, which revolve beyond the scope of words, can only be unfolded through practice alone.

body.translated_text: This path has been laid open by means of a measured treatment, compressing the endless expanse of ornaments;

body.text: ity ācāryadaṇḍinaḥ kṛtau kāvyādarśe 'rthālaṅkāravibhāgo nāma dvitīyo paricchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter, named 'The Division of Sense-Ornaments' (<s>Arthālaṅkāravibhāga</s>), in the <s>Kāvyādarśa</s> composed by the teacher <s>Daṇḍin</s>.
